## prime_hunt/src/intrinsic.rs
```rust
//! Intrinsic CRAM Address — The Number's Position Outside of Time
//!
//! Every integer n has a fixed address on the multi-head CRAM torus.
//! This address is INTRINSIC — it depends only on n, not on any gap,
//! range, scanning order, or calibration window.
//!
//! Each Hydra head probes n from a different angle:
//!   Head A: root(n mod p, 1) — additive unit probe (shift by 1)
//!   Head B: root(n mod p, n mod p) — self-interaction (quadratic character)
//!   Head C: root(n mod p, p-1) — boundary probe (distance to modular edge)
//!
//! The multi-head CRAM address IS the number's position in the coprime
//! lattice. Primes live at specific addresses. That distribution is
//! a static mathematical object — an atlas computed once, valid forever.
//!
//! The atlas is OUTSIDE OF TIME: it doesn't depend on which numbers
//! you've seen, what range you're searching, or what order you scan.
//! It's a property of the integers themselves under CRAM projection.
//!
//! The DIMENSION is the number of (head × lane × post) coordinates.
//! Each coordinate is a carry bit. More heads = higher dimension =
//! finer resolution of the coprime lattice.

use crate::coprime_families::{CramTopology, Lane, Root, Post};
use crate::crt;

// ── Modular arithmetic ──────────────────────────────────────────────

fn addmod(a: u64, b: u64, m: u64) -> u64 { ((a as u128 + b as u128) % m as u128) as u64 }
fn submod(a: u64, b: u64, m: u64) -> u64 { if a >= b { (a-b) % m } else { m - ((b-a) % m) } }
fn mulmod(a: u64, b: u64, m: u64) -> u64 { ((a as u128 * b as u128) % m as u128) as u64 }

fn is_prime_u64(n: u64) -> bool {
    if n < 2 { return false; } if n < 4 { return true; }
    if n % 2 == 0 || n % 3 == 0 { return false; }
    let mut i = 5u64;
    while i.saturating_mul(i) <= n { if n % i == 0 || n % (i+2) == 0 { return false; } i += 6; }
    true
}

// ── Intrinsic Probe Types ───────────────────────────────────────────

/// What does the root operator's second argument come from?
/// This is what makes the address INTRINSIC — no external gap needed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Probe {
    /// root(n mod p, 1) — unit shift: how does n respond to +1, -1, ×1?
    Unit,
    /// root(n mod p, n mod p) — self-interaction: n's quadratic character
    Self_,
    /// root(n mod p, p-1 mod p) — edge probe: n's distance from modular boundary
    Edge,
    /// root(n mod p, 2 mod p) — parity probe: n's relationship to 2
    Parity,
    /// Pure residue: just n mod p, no root operator, post only
    Residue,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Probe {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Probe::Unit => write!(f, "Unit"),
            Probe::Self_ => write!(f, "Self"),
            Probe::Edge => write!(f, "Edge"),
            Probe::Parity => write!(f, "Par"),
            Probe::Residue => write!(f, "Res"),
        }
    }
}

/// One dimension of the intrinsic address: (prime, probe, root_op, post_op) → carry bit
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Dimension {
    pub prime: u64,
    pub probe: Probe,
    pub root: Root,
    pub post: Post,
}

impl Dimension {
    /// Compute this dimension's value for integer n. Returns carry bit (0 or 1).
    pub fn evaluate(&self, n: u64) -> u8 {
        let p = self.prime;
        let n_r = n % p;

        // Determine second operand based on probe type
        let b_r = match self.probe {
            Probe::Unit    => 1u64 % p,
            Probe::Self_   => n_r,
            Probe::Edge    => (p - 1) % p,
            Probe::Parity  => 2u64 % p,
            Probe::Residue => 0, // unused for Residue probe
        };

        // Apply root operator (or skip for Residue probe)
        let inter = if self.probe == Probe::Residue {
            n_r
        } else {
            match self.root {
                Root::Add => addmod(n_r, b_r, p),
                Root::Sub => submod(n_r, b_r, p),
                Root::Mul => mulmod(n_r, b_r, p),
                Root::Div => {
                    if b_r == 0 { 0 }
                    else { crate::coprime_families::mod_inv_pub(b_r, p).map(|inv| mulmod(n_r, inv, p)).unwrap_or(0) }
                }
            }
        };

        // Apply post-processor
        let out = match self.post {
            Post::Id  => inter,
            Post::Neg => if inter == 0 { 0 } else { p - inter },
            Post::Sqr => mulmod(inter, inter, p),
            Post::Inv => {
                if inter == 0 { 0 }
                else { crate::coprime_families::mod_inv_pub(inter, p).unwrap_or(0) }
            }
        };

        // Carry bit: threshold at p/2
        if out * 2 >= p { 1 } else { 0 }
    }
}

// ── Intrinsic Address ───────────────────────────────────────────────

/// The full CRAM address of a number: a binary vector across all dimensions.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct Address {
    pub bits: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Address {
    pub fn to_id(&self) -> u64 {
        let mut id = 0u64;
        for (i, &bit) in self.bits.iter().enumerate() {
            if i >= 64 { break; }
            id |= (bit as u64) << i;
        }
        id
    }

    pub fn dim(&self) -> usize { self.bits.len() }
}

// ── Address Space: The Multi-Dimensional CRAM Torus ─────────────────

/// The address space: a set of dimensions that define the CRAM torus.
/// Every integer has a unique address in this space.
pub struct AddressSpace {
    pub dimensions: Vec<Dimension>,
    pub modulus: u64, // LCM of all primes (defines the period)
}

impl AddressSpace {
    pub fn new(dimensions: Vec<Dimension>) -> Self {
        let mut modulus = 1u64;
        let mut seen_primes = Vec::new();
        for dim in &dimensions {
            if !seen_primes.contains(&dim.prime) {
                modulus *= dim.prime;
                seen_primes.push(dim.prime);
            }
        }
        Self { dimensions, modulus }
    }

    pub fn ndim(&self) -> usize { self.dimensions.len() }

    /// Compute the intrinsic address of n. O(ndim) integer operations.
    pub fn address_of(&self, n: u64) -> Address {
        Address {
            bits: self.dimensions.iter().map(|d| d.evaluate(n)).collect()
        }
    }

    /// Check if n is coprime to the modulus (in the coprime lattice).
    pub fn is_coprime(&self, n: u64) -> bool {
        crt::gcd(n as u128, self.modulus as u128) == 1
    }

    /// The address is PERIODIC with period = modulus.
    /// address_of(n) == address_of(n + k * modulus) for all k.
    /// This is the "outside of time" property.
    pub fn period(&self) -> u64 { self.modulus }
}

// ── Pre-built Address Spaces ────────────────────────────────────────

/// Build a rich multi-probe address space on the safe basis {3,5,7,11,13}.
pub fn build_full_address_space() -> AddressSpace {
    let primes = [3u64, 5, 7, 11, 13];
    let probes = [Probe::Unit, Probe::Self_, Probe::Edge, Probe::Residue];
    let posts = [Post::Id, Post::Sqr];

    let mut dims = Vec::new();
    for &p in &primes {
        for &probe in &probes {
            let root = match probe {
                Probe::Residue => Root::Add, // unused but needed
                Probe::Self_   => Root::Mul, // n × n = Sqr
                _              => Root::Add, // default
            };
            for &post in &posts {
                dims.push(Dimension { prime: p, probe, root, post });
            }
        }
    }
    // 5 primes × 4 probes × 2 posts = 40 dimensions → 2^40 addresses (1 trillion)
    // Too many — trim to the most discriminative
    // Use: Unit+Id, Unit+Sqr, Self+Sqr, Residue+Id, Residue+Sqr per prime = 25 dims
    let mut trimmed = Vec::new();
    for &p in &primes {
        trimmed.push(Dimension { prime: p, probe: Probe::Unit, root: Root::Add, post: Post::Id });
        trimmed.push(Dimension { prime: p, probe: Probe::Unit, root: Root::Sub, post: Post::Sqr });
        trimmed.push(Dimension { prime: p, probe: Probe::Self_, root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Sqr });
        trimmed.push(Dimension { prime: p, probe: Probe::Residue, root: Root::Add, post: Post::Id });
        trimmed.push(Dimension { prime: p, probe: Probe::Edge, root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr });
    }
    AddressSpace::new(trimmed) // 25 dimensions
}

/// Compact space: fewer dimensions, manageable stratum count.
pub fn build_compact_address_space() -> AddressSpace {
    let primes = [3u64, 5, 7, 11, 13];
    let mut dims = Vec::new();
    for &p in &primes {
        // 3 dimensions per prime: Residue+Id, Unit+Sqr, Self+Sqr
        dims.push(Dimension { prime: p, probe: Probe::Residue, root: Root::Add, post: Post::Id });
        dims.push(Dimension { prime: p, probe: Probe::Unit, root: Root::Sub, post: Post::Sqr });
        dims.push(Dimension { prime: p, probe: Probe::Self_, root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Sqr });
    }
    AddressSpace::new(dims) // 15 dimensions → 32768 addresses
}

// ── Address Atlas: The Eternal Map ──────────────────────────────────

/// The atlas: prime density at every address, computed once.
/// Since addresses are periodic (period = modulus), the atlas is finite.
/// Every coprime residue class mod M has a fixed address.
/// The atlas maps address → prime density (measured or predicted).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct AddressAtlas {
    pub space_ndim: usize,
    pub modulus: u64,
    pub entries: std::collections::HashMap<u64, AtlasEntry>,
    pub total_addresses: u32,
    pub prime_rich_threshold: f64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct AtlasEntry {
    pub address_id: u64,
    pub coprime_count: u32,
    pub prime_count: u32,
    pub density: f64,
    pub is_prime_rich: bool,
}

impl AddressAtlas {
    /// Build the atlas by scanning one full period [2, modulus + sample_range).
    /// Since addresses repeat with period = modulus, scanning one period
    /// gives complete coverage. Additional range adds statistics.
    pub fn build(space: &AddressSpace, scan_limit: u64, threshold_percentile: f64) -> Self {
        let mut entries: std::collections::HashMap<u64, (u32, u32)> = std::collections::HashMap::new();

        for n in 2..scan_limit {
            if !space.is_coprime(n) { continue; }
            let addr = space.address_of(n);
            let id = addr.to_id();
            let entry = entries.entry(id).or_insert((0, 0));
            entry.0 += 1;
            if is_prime_u64(n) { entry.1 += 1; }
        }

        // Compute densities
        let mut atlas_entries: Vec<(u64, f64)> = entries.iter()
            .map(|(&id, &(cc, pc))| (id, if cc > 0 { pc as f64 / cc as f64 } else { 0.0 }))
            .collect();
        atlas_entries.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap());

        // Threshold: capture top percentile of primes
        let total_primes: u32 = entries.values().map(|v| v.1).sum();
        let target = (total_primes as f64 * threshold_percentile) as u32;
        let mut captured = 0u32;
        let mut threshold = 0.0f64;
        let mut rich_ids = std::collections::HashSet::new();

        for &(id, density) in &atlas_entries {
            let pc = entries[&id].1;
            if captured < target || threshold_percentile >= 0.999 {
                captured += pc;
                threshold = density;
                rich_ids.insert(id);
            }
        }

        let final_entries = entries.into_iter().map(|(id, (cc, pc))| {
            let density = if cc > 0 { pc as f64 / cc as f64 } else { 0.0 };
            (id, AtlasEntry {
                address_id: id,
                coprime_count: cc,
                prime_count: pc,
                density,
                is_prime_rich: rich_ids.contains(&id),
            })
        }).collect();

        AddressAtlas {
            space_ndim: space.ndim(),
            modulus: space.period(),
            entries: final_entries,
            total_addresses: atlas_entries.len() as u32,
            prime_rich_threshold: threshold,
        }
    }

    /// Query: is this address prime-rich?
    pub fn is_prime_rich(&self, addr_id: u64) -> bool {
        self.entries.get(&addr_id).map(|e| e.is_prime_rich).unwrap_or(true)
        // Unknown addresses default to "test" (safe)
    }

    pub fn prime_rich_count(&self) -> u32 {
        self.entries.values().filter(|e| e.is_prime_rich).count() as u32
    }

    pub fn prime_poor_count(&self) -> u32 {
        self.entries.values().filter(|e| !e.is_prime_rich).count() as u32
    }

    /// Gini coefficient of prime density across addresses
    pub fn gini(&self) -> f64 {
        let densities: Vec<f64> = self.entries.values()
            .filter(|e| e.coprime_count > 0)
            .map(|e| e.density)
            .collect();
        if densities.is_empty() { return 0.0; }
        let n = densities.len() as f64;
        let mean = densities.iter().sum::<f64>() / n;
        if mean == 0.0 { return 0.0; }
        let abs_diff: f64 = densities.iter()
            .flat_map(|&a| densities.iter().map(move |&b| (a - b).abs()))
            .sum();
        abs_diff / (2.0 * n * n * mean)
    }
}

/// The eternal hunt: compute address → check atlas → test or skip.
/// Works for ANY n, in ANY order, with NO calibration per range.
pub fn eternal_hunt(
    space: &AddressSpace,
    atlas: &AddressAtlas,
    start: u64,
    limit: u64,
) -> EternalHuntResult {
    let mut primes_found = Vec::new();
    let mut tested = 0u64;
    let mut skipped = 0u64;
    let mut false_negatives = 0u64;
    let mut coprimes = 0u64;

    for n in start.max(2)..limit {
        if !space.is_coprime(n) { continue; }
        coprimes += 1;

        let addr = space.address_of(n);
        let addr_id = addr.to_id();

        if atlas.is_prime_rich(addr_id) {
            tested += 1;
            if is_prime_u64(n) { primes_found.push(n); }
        } else {
            skipped += 1;
            if is_prime_u64(n) { false_negatives += 1; }
        }
    }

    let actual = primes_found.len() as u64 + false_negatives;
    EternalHuntResult {
        primes_found,
        coprimes,
        tested,
        skipped,
        false_negatives,
        recall: if actual > 0 { (actual - false_negatives) as f64 / actual as f64 } else { 1.0 },
        speedup: if tested > 0 { coprimes as f64 / tested as f64 } else { 1.0 },
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct EternalHuntResult {
    pub primes_found: Vec<u64>,
    pub coprimes: u64,
    pub tested: u64,
    pub skipped: u64,
    pub false_negatives: u64,
    pub recall: f64,
    pub speedup: f64,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_address_periodicity() {
        let space = build_compact_address_space();
        let m = space.period();
        // Address of n must equal address of n + m
        for n in [17u64, 29, 97, 101, 1009] {
            let a1 = space.address_of(n);
            let a2 = space.address_of(n + m);
            assert_eq!(a1, a2, "Address not periodic for n={}", n);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_address_deterministic() {
        let space = build_compact_address_space();
        // Same n always gives same address
        let a1 = space.address_of(97);
        let a2 = space.address_of(97);
        assert_eq!(a1, a2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_atlas_build() {
        let space = build_compact_address_space();
        let atlas = AddressAtlas::build(&space, 10_000, 0.95);
        assert!(atlas.total_addresses > 0);
        assert!(atlas.prime_rich_count() > 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_eternal_hunt_finds_primes() {
        let space = build_compact_address_space();
        let atlas = AddressAtlas::build(&space, 10_000, 1.00);
        let result = eternal_hunt(&space, &atlas, 10_000, 20_000);
        assert!(!result.primes_found.is_empty());
        for &p in &result.primes_found {
            assert!(is_prime_u64(p));
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Monoid M_H: The multiplicative monoid of the zero-shadow locus.
//!
//! M_H = { n : gcd(n, 730730) = 1 }
//! where 730730 = 2 × 5 × 7 × 11 × 13 × 73
//!
//! Irreducible elements of M_H = "good primes" = primes coprime to 730730
//! Composite elements of M_H = "polluted composites"
//!
//! Test: Does this characterization yield anything beyond a standard sieve step?

use crate::crt::{gcd, factorize, is_prime, mod_pow, ramanujan_sum_prime};
use crate::shadow::S_R;
use crate::helical::CR;

/// The full coprimeness modulus.
/// M = 2 × 5 × 7 × 11 × 13 × 73 = 730730
/// Note: 3 is NOT in M because 3 ∤ CR and 3 ∉ S_R.
pub const M_COPRIME: u128 = 2 * 5 * 7 * 11 * 13 * 73;

/// Prime factors of M
pub const M_FACTORS: [u128; 6] = [2, 5, 7, 11, 13, 73];

/// Test membership in M_H: n is in the monoid iff gcd(n, M) = 1
pub fn in_monoid(n: u128) -> bool {
    n > 0 && gcd(n, M_COPRIME) == 1
}

/// Shadow entropy: sum of Ramanujan sums c_q(n) for q ∈ S_R
pub fn shadow_entropy(n: u128) -> i128 {
    S_R.iter().map(|&q| ramanujan_sum_prime(q, n)).sum()
}

/// Classify an element of M_H
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MonoidClass {
    /// Not in M_H
    Outside,
    /// Irreducible generator (prime coprime to M)
    GoodPrime,
    /// Composite element with at least one factor ≤ 13 (e.g., 27=3³)
    PollutedComposite,
    /// Composite element with all factors > 13 (e.g., 289=17²)
    PureCompositeCoprimeBelow13,
    /// The number 1 (identity element)
    Identity,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for MonoidClass {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            MonoidClass::Outside => write!(f, "OUTSIDE"),
            MonoidClass::GoodPrime => write!(f, "GOOD_PRIME"),
            MonoidClass::PollutedComposite => write!(f, "POLLUTED"),
            MonoidClass::PureCompositeCoprimeBelow13 => write!(f, "PURE_COMPOSITE"),
            MonoidClass::Identity => write!(f, "IDENTITY"),
        }
    }
}

pub fn classify_monoid(n: u128) -> MonoidClass {
    if n == 1 { return MonoidClass::Identity; }
    if !in_monoid(n) { return MonoidClass::Outside; }
    if is_prime(n) { return MonoidClass::GoodPrime; }

    // Composite in M_H — check if any factor is ≤ 13
    // Factors of M are {2,5,7,11,13,73}. Since gcd(n,M)=1, n is coprime
    // to all of those. But n might have factor 3 (not in M).
    let factors = factorize(n);
    let has_small_factor = factors.iter().any(|&(p, _)| p <= 13);
    if has_small_factor {
        MonoidClass::PollutedComposite
    } else {
        MonoidClass::PureCompositeCoprimeBelow13
    }
}

/// Enumerate M_H elements in [lo, hi] with classification.
pub fn enumerate_monoid(lo: u128, hi: u128) -> MonoidCensus {
    let mut census = MonoidCensus {
        range: (lo, hi),
        total: 0,
        good_primes: Vec::new(),
        polluted: Vec::new(),
        pure_composites: Vec::new(),
        outside: 0,
    };

    for n in lo..=hi {
        match classify_monoid(n) {
            MonoidClass::Outside => census.outside += 1,
            MonoidClass::GoodPrime => {
                census.total += 1;
                census.good_primes.push(n);
            }
            MonoidClass::PollutedComposite => {
                census.total += 1;
                census.polluted.push(n);
            }
            MonoidClass::PureCompositeCoprimeBelow13 => {
                census.total += 1;
                census.pure_composites.push(n);
            }
            MonoidClass::Identity => census.total += 1,
        }
    }
    census
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MonoidCensus {
    pub range: (u128, u128),
    pub total: u128,
    pub good_primes: Vec<u128>,
    pub polluted: Vec<u128>,
    pub pure_composites: Vec<u128>,
    pub outside: u128,
}

/// Exponential reach test: compute b^k, verify monoid membership,
/// return helical coordinates.
pub fn exponential_reach(base: u128, max_exp: u32) -> Vec<ExpReachPoint> {
    assert!(in_monoid(base), "Base {} not in monoid", base);

    let mut results = Vec::new();
    let mut power = 1u128;

    for k in 1..=max_exp {
        // Use checked multiplication to detect overflow
        power = match power.checked_mul(base) {
            Some(v) => v,
            None => break, // overflow
        };

        let theta = power % CR;
        let big_k = power / CR;
        let entropy = shadow_entropy(power);
        let coprime_cr = gcd(power, CR) == 1;
        let coprime_m = gcd(power, M_COPRIME) == 1;
        let prime = if power < 1_000_000 { is_prime(power) } else { false }; // skip expensive check for huge

        results.push(ExpReachPoint {
            base,
            exponent: k,
            value: power,
            theta,
            winding_k: big_k,
            entropy,
            coprime_cr,
            coprime_m,
            is_prime: prime,
            class: classify_monoid(power),
        });
    }
    results
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ExpReachPoint {
    pub base: u128,
    pub exponent: u32,
    pub value: u128,
    pub theta: u128,
    pub winding_k: u128,
    pub entropy: i128,
    pub coprime_cr: bool,
    pub coprime_m: bool,
    pub is_prime: bool,
    pub class: MonoidClass,
}

/// Modular exponential reach: compute θ = b^k mod CR without computing b^k.
/// This is the O(log k) fast path.
pub fn modular_exp_reach(base: u128, exponent: u128) -> u128 {
    mod_pow(base % CR, exponent, CR)
}

/// Algorithm 1 test: the κ-filter from the document.
/// κ = (θ - v_anchor) · L⁻¹ mod 17
/// Claim: |κ| ≤ 1 and irreducible → prime
pub fn algorithm1_test(n: u128, v_anchor: u128) -> Alg1Result {
    if !in_monoid(n) {
        return Alg1Result {
            n, theta: 0, kappa: 0, passes_kappa: false,
            is_irreducible: false, predicted_prime: false, actual_prime: false,
        };
    }

    let theta = n % CR;
    // κ = (θ - v_anchor) · L⁻¹ mod 17
    // L = CR = 18980
    // Need L⁻¹ mod 17: 18980 mod 17 = 18980 - 1116*17 = 18980 - 18972 = 8
    // 8⁻¹ mod 17: 8*15 = 120 = 7*17+1, so 8⁻¹ = 15
    let l_inv_mod_17 = 15u128; // 18980⁻¹ mod 17

    let diff = if theta >= v_anchor {
        (theta - v_anchor) % 17
    } else {
        (17 - ((v_anchor - theta) % 17)) % 17
    };
    let kappa = (diff * l_inv_mod_17) % 17;

    // Map to signed: if kappa > 8, it's "negative"
    let kappa_signed = if kappa > 8 { kappa as i128 - 17 } else { kappa as i128 };
    let passes_kappa = kappa_signed.abs() <= 1;

    // Check irreducibility (= primality for elements of M_H that are prime)
    let actual_prime = is_prime(n);
    let is_irreducible = actual_prime; // In M_H, irreducible ⟺ prime

    let predicted_prime = passes_kappa && is_irreducible;

    Alg1Result {
        n,
        theta,
        kappa: kappa_signed,
        passes_kappa,
        is_irreducible,
        predicted_prime,
        actual_prime,
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Alg1Result {
    pub n: u128,
    pub theta: u128,
    pub kappa: i128,
    pub passes_kappa: bool,
    pub is_irreducible: bool,
    pub predicted_prime: bool,
    pub actual_prime: bool,
}

/// The critical test: Does the κ-filter actually help?
/// Compare Algorithm 1 predictions vs simple monoid membership.
pub fn algorithm1_bulk_test(limit: u128, v_anchor: u128) -> Alg1BulkResult {
    let mut true_pos = 0u32;   // predicted prime AND is prime
    let mut false_pos = 0u32;  // predicted prime AND NOT prime
    let mut true_neg = 0u32;   // predicted NOT prime AND NOT prime
    let mut false_neg = 0u32;  // predicted NOT prime AND IS prime
    let mut kappa_passes = 0u32;
    let mut kappa_passes_prime = 0u32;
    let mut kappa_passes_composite = 0u32;
    let mut total_in_monoid = 0u32;
    let mut total_primes = 0u32;
    let mut total_composites = 0u32;

    // Kappa distribution
    let mut kappa_hist = [0u32; 17];

    for n in 2..=limit {
        if !in_monoid(n) { continue; }
        total_in_monoid += 1;

        let result = algorithm1_test(n, v_anchor);
        let prime = result.actual_prime;

        if prime { total_primes += 1; } else { total_composites += 1; }

        // Track kappa distribution
        let k_idx = ((result.kappa % 17 + 17) % 17) as usize;
        kappa_hist[k_idx] += 1;

        if result.passes_kappa {
            kappa_passes += 1;
            if prime { kappa_passes_prime += 1; } else { kappa_passes_composite += 1; }
        }

        // Algorithm 1 uses kappa AND irreducibility
        // But irreducibility IS primality, so this is circular
        // Instead, test: does kappa alone filter?
        match (result.passes_kappa, prime) {
            (true, true) => true_pos += 1,
            (true, false) => false_pos += 1,
            (false, false) => true_neg += 1,
            (false, true) => false_neg += 1,
        }
    }

    Alg1BulkResult {
        limit,
        total_in_monoid,
        total_primes,
        total_composites,
        kappa_passes,
        kappa_passes_prime,
        kappa_passes_composite,
        true_pos,
        false_pos,
        true_neg,
        false_neg,
        kappa_hist,
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Alg1BulkResult {
    pub limit: u128,
    pub total_in_monoid: u32,
    pub total_primes: u32,
    pub total_composites: u32,
    pub kappa_passes: u32,
    pub kappa_passes_prime: u32,
    pub kappa_passes_composite: u32,
    pub true_pos: u32,
    pub false_pos: u32,
    pub true_neg: u32,
    pub false_neg: u32,
    pub kappa_hist: [u32; 17],
}

/// Multiplicative closure test: verify that products of monoid elements stay in monoid.
pub fn closure_test(elements: &[u128]) -> ClosureResult {
    let mut tested = 0u32;
    let mut passed = 0u32;
    let mut failed = Vec::new();

    for i in 0..elements.len() {
        for j in i..elements.len() {
            let product = match elements[i].checked_mul(elements[j]) {
                Some(v) => v,
                None => continue,
            };
            tested += 1;
            if in_monoid(product) {
                passed += 1;
            } else {
                failed.push((elements[i], elements[j], product));
            }
        }
    }

    ClosureResult { tested, passed, failed }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ClosureResult {
    pub tested: u32,
    pub passed: u32,
    pub failed: Vec<(u128, u128, u128)>,
}

/// Density analysis: what fraction of M_H at winding K are prime?
pub fn density_by_winding(max_k: u32) -> Vec<(u32, u32, u32, f64)> {
    let mut results = Vec::new();

    for k in 0..max_k {
        let lo = k as u128 * CR;
        let hi = lo + CR - 1;
        let mut primes = 0u32;
        let mut in_mon = 0u32;

        for n in lo..=hi {
            if n < 2 { continue; }
            if in_monoid(n) {
                in_mon += 1;
                if is_prime(n) {
                    primes += 1;
                }
            }
        }

        let density = if in_mon > 0 { primes as f64 / in_mon as f64 } else { 0.0 };
        results.push((k, primes, in_mon, density));
    }
    results
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_m_coprime_factorization() {
        assert_eq!(M_COPRIME, 730730);
        assert_eq!(factorize(M_COPRIME), vec![
            (2, 1), (5, 1), (7, 1), (11, 1), (13, 1), (73, 1)
        ]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_3_not_in_m() {
        // 3 is NOT a factor of M, so 3 IS in the monoid
        assert!(in_monoid(3));
        assert!(in_monoid(9));
        assert!(in_monoid(27));
        // But 2, 5, 7, 11, 13, 73 are NOT in the monoid
        assert!(!in_monoid(2));
        assert!(!in_monoid(5));
        assert!(!in_monoid(7));
        assert!(!in_monoid(11));
        assert!(!in_monoid(13));
        assert!(!in_monoid(73));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_monoid_classification() {
        assert_eq!(classify_monoid(17), MonoidClass::GoodPrime);
        assert_eq!(classify_monoid(19), MonoidClass::GoodPrime);
        assert_eq!(classify_monoid(27), MonoidClass::PollutedComposite); // 3³, has factor ≤ 13
        assert_eq!(classify_monoid(289), MonoidClass::PureCompositeCoprimeBelow13); // 17²
        assert_eq!(classify_monoid(323), MonoidClass::PureCompositeCoprimeBelow13); // 17×19
        assert_eq!(classify_monoid(10), MonoidClass::Outside); // 2×5
        assert_eq!(classify_monoid(1), MonoidClass::Identity);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_monoid_closure() {
        // 27 × 17 = 459
        assert!(in_monoid(459));
        assert_eq!(shadow_entropy(459), -3);
        assert_eq!(gcd(459, CR), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_exponential_reach_27() {
        let points = exponential_reach(27, 5);
        assert_eq!(points.len(), 5);
        assert_eq!(points[0].value, 27);
        assert_eq!(points[0].theta, 27);
        assert!(points[0].coprime_m);
        assert_eq!(points[1].value, 729);
        assert_eq!(points[1].theta, 729);
        assert!(points[1].coprime_m);
        assert_eq!(points[2].value, 19683);
        assert_eq!(points[2].theta, 19683 % CR); // 703
        assert!(points[2].coprime_m);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_modular_exp_fast() {
        // 27^5 mod 18980
        let theta_fast = modular_exp_reach(27, 5);
        let theta_slow = 14348907u128 % CR; // 27^5 = 14348907
        assert_eq!(theta_fast, theta_slow);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_73_excluded() {
        // 73 is a factor of CR (18980 = 4×5×13×73), so gcd(73, CR) = 73
        assert!(!in_monoid(73));
        assert_eq!(gcd(73, CR), 73);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_shadow_entropy_monoid() {
        // All monoid elements should have entropy = -3
        for n in 2..500u128 {
            if in_monoid(n) {
                assert_eq!(shadow_entropy(n), -3,
                    "n={} in monoid but entropy={}", n, shadow_entropy(n));
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Multi-Headed Coprime Family Analyzer
//!
//! Each Hydra head is a DIFFERENT CRAM lens on the coprime lattice.
//! The multi-head carry signature (concatenation of all heads' patterns)
//! is the high-dimensional fingerprint that resolves coprime family structure.
//!
//! Single head (5 lanes): 2⁵ = 32 strata
//! Two heads:             32 × 32 = 1,024 strata
//! Three heads:           32 × 32 × 32 = 32,768 strata
//!
//! Each head can be tuned to see different structure:
//! - Head A: gap-2 (twin) topology → sees twin-pair symmetry
//! - Head B: gap-6 (sexy) topology → sees sexy-pair symmetry
//! - Head C: S⁶ champion → sees maximal CRAM distortion
//! - Head D: Mul+Id everywhere → sees multiplicative structure
//! The INTERSECTION of their views reveals what no single head can.

use crate::coprime_families::{
    CramTopology, Lane, Root, Post, Champions,
};
use crate::crt;

/// A single Hydra head: one CRAM topology producing one carry pattern per input.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Head {
    pub label: String,
    pub topology: CramTopology,
    pub target_gap: u64,  // what this head is tuned to observe
}

impl Head {
    pub fn new(label: &str, topology: CramTopology, target_gap: u64) -> Self {
        Self { label: label.to_string(), topology, target_gap }
    }

    /// Compute this head's carry pattern for element n.
    pub fn observe(&self, n: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.topology.carry_pattern(n, self.target_gap)
    }

    pub fn k(&self) -> usize { self.topology.k() }
}

/// Multi-head carry signature: concatenation of all heads' patterns.
/// This is the high-dimensional fingerprint in the coprime lattice.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct MultiSignature {
    pub bits: Vec<u8>,
    pub total_lanes: usize,
}

impl MultiSignature {
    pub fn to_id(&self) -> u64 {
        let mut id = 0u64;
        for (i, &bit) in self.bits.iter().enumerate() {
            if i >= 64 { break; } // cap at 64 bits
            id |= (bit as u64) << i;
        }
        id
    }

    pub fn to_string_compact(&self) -> String {
        self.bits.iter().map(|&b| if b == 1 { '1' } else { '0' }).collect()
    }
}

/// The Multi-Headed Hydra: multiple CRAM lenses observing simultaneously.
pub struct MultiHydra {
    pub heads: Vec<Head>,
    pub total_lanes: usize,
    pub total_strata: u64,  // 2^total_lanes (theoretical max)
}

impl MultiHydra {
    pub fn new(heads: Vec<Head>) -> Self {
        let total_lanes: usize = heads.iter().map(|h| h.k()).sum();
        let total_strata = if total_lanes <= 20 { 1u64 << total_lanes } else { 0 }; // cap display
        Self { heads, total_lanes, total_strata }
    }

    /// Compute the full multi-head signature for element n.
    pub fn observe(&self, n: u64) -> MultiSignature {
        let mut bits = Vec::with_capacity(self.total_lanes);
        for head in &self.heads {
            bits.extend_from_slice(&head.observe(n));
        }
        MultiSignature { bits, total_lanes: self.total_lanes }
    }

    /// Map the coprime lattice: for each coprime n in [start, limit),
    /// compute multi-signature and bin by stratum.
    pub fn map_lattice(&self, start: u64, limit: u64) -> LatticeMap {
        let modulus = self.heads.iter()
            .map(|h| h.topology.modulus)
            .fold(1u64, |acc, m| {
                // Use LCM since heads may share primes
                let g = crt::gcd(acc as u128, m as u128) as u64;
                acc / g * m
            });

        let mut strata: std::collections::HashMap<u64, StratumData> = std::collections::HashMap::new();
        let mut total_coprimes = 0u32;
        let mut total_primes = 0u32;

        let is_prime = |n: u64| -> bool {
            if n < 2 { return false; } if n < 4 { return true; }
            if n % 2 == 0 || n % 3 == 0 { return false; }
            let mut i = 5u64;
            while i.saturating_mul(i) <= n {
                if n % i == 0 || n % (i+2) == 0 { return false; } i += 6;
            }
            true
        };

        for n in start.max(2)..limit {
            // Must be coprime to ALL head moduli
            let coprime = self.heads.iter().all(|h|
                crt::gcd(n as u128, h.topology.modulus as u128) == 1
            );
            if !coprime { continue; }

            total_coprimes += 1;
            let sig = self.observe(n);
            let sig_id = sig.to_id();
            let is_p = is_prime(n);
            if is_p { total_primes += 1; }

            let entry = strata.entry(sig_id).or_insert_with(|| StratumData {
                signature: sig.to_string_compact(),
                coprime_count: 0, prime_count: 0, composite_count: 0,
            });
            entry.coprime_count += 1;
            if is_p { entry.prime_count += 1; } else { entry.composite_count += 1; }
        }

        // Convert to sorted vec
        let mut stratum_vec: Vec<(u64, StratumData)> = strata.into_iter().collect();
        stratum_vec.sort_by(|a, b| {
            let da = a.1.prime_density();
            let db = b.1.prime_density();
            db.partial_cmp(&da).unwrap()
        });

        let populated = stratum_vec.len() as u32;
        let avg_density = if total_coprimes > 0 {
            total_primes as f64 / total_coprimes as f64
        } else { 0.0 };

        // Gini
        let densities: Vec<f64> = stratum_vec.iter()
            .filter(|(_, d)| d.coprime_count > 0)
            .map(|(_, d)| d.prime_density())
            .collect();
        let gini = compute_gini(&densities);

        // Spread
        let max_d = densities.iter().copied().fold(0.0f64, f64::max);
        let min_d = densities.iter().copied().fold(1.0f64, f64::min);

        LatticeMap {
            total_coprimes,
            total_primes,
            populated_strata: populated,
            theoretical_strata: self.total_strata,
            strata: stratum_vec,
            avg_density,
            gini,
            density_spread: max_d - min_d,
            total_lanes: self.total_lanes,
            head_count: self.heads.len(),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StratumData {
    pub signature: String,
    pub coprime_count: u32,
    pub prime_count: u32,
    pub composite_count: u32,
}

impl StratumData {
    pub fn prime_density(&self) -> f64 {
        if self.coprime_count > 0 { self.prime_count as f64 / self.coprime_count as f64 }
        else { 0.0 }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct LatticeMap {
    pub total_coprimes: u32,
    pub total_primes: u32,
    pub populated_strata: u32,
    pub theoretical_strata: u64,
    pub strata: Vec<(u64, StratumData)>,
    pub avg_density: f64,
    pub gini: f64,
    pub density_spread: f64,
    pub total_lanes: usize,
    pub head_count: usize,
}

fn compute_gini(values: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    if values.is_empty() { return 0.0; }
    let n = values.len() as f64;
    let mean = values.iter().sum::<f64>() / n;
    if mean == 0.0 { return 0.0; }
    let abs_diff: f64 = values.iter()
        .flat_map(|&a| values.iter().map(move |&b| (a - b).abs()))
        .sum();
    abs_diff / (2.0 * n * n * mean)
}

// ── Pre-built Multi-Hydra Configurations ────────────────────────────

pub fn build_twin_hydra() -> MultiHydra {
    MultiHydra::new(vec![
        Head::new("Twin-Mul", CramTopology::new(vec![
            Lane { prime: 3,  root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
            Lane { prime: 5,  root: Root::Sub, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 7,  root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 11, root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 13, root: Root::Sub, post: Post::Id },
        ]), 2),
        Head::new("QR-Sqr", CramTopology::new(vec![
            Lane { prime: 3,  root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 5,  root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 7,  root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 11, root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 13, root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
        ]), 2),
        Head::new("Mul-Struct", CramTopology::new(vec![
            Lane { prime: 3,  root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
            Lane { prime: 5,  root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
            Lane { prime: 7,  root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
            Lane { prime: 11, root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
            Lane { prime: 13, root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
        ]), 2),
    ])
}

pub fn build_multi_gap_hydra() -> MultiHydra {
    MultiHydra::new(vec![
        Head::new("Gap2-Twin", Champions::twin(), 2),
        Head::new("Gap6-Sexy", CramTopology::new(vec![
            Lane { prime: 3,  root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
            Lane { prime: 5,  root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 7,  root: Root::Sub, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 11, root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 13, root: Root::Add, post: Post::Id },
        ]), 6),
        Head::new("Gap30-Deep", CramTopology::new(vec![
            Lane { prime: 3,  root: Root::Sub, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 5,  root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },  // 5|30 → Mul sees zero structure
            Lane { prime: 7,  root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
            Lane { prime: 11, root: Root::Sub, post: Post::Neg },
            Lane { prime: 13, root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
        ]), 30),
    ])
}

/// Progressive Hydra: add heads one at a time to measure resolution gain.
pub fn build_progressive(gap: u64) -> Vec<(String, MultiHydra)> {
    let head_a = Head::new("A:Twin", Champions::twin(), gap);
    let head_b = Head::new("B:QR", CramTopology::new(vec![
        Lane { prime: 3,  root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
        Lane { prime: 5,  root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
        Lane { prime: 7,  root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
        Lane { prime: 11, root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
        Lane { prime: 13, root: Root::Add, post: Post::Sqr },
    ]), gap);
    let head_c = Head::new("C:Mul", CramTopology::new(vec![
        Lane { prime: 3,  root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
        Lane { prime: 5,  root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
        Lane { prime: 7,  root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
        Lane { prime: 11, root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
        Lane { prime: 13, root: Root::Mul, post: Post::Id },
    ]), gap);

    vec![
        ("1-head (A)".into(), MultiHydra::new(vec![head_a.clone()])),
        ("2-head (A+B)".into(), MultiHydra::new(vec![head_a.clone(), head_b.clone()])),
        ("3-head (A+B+C)".into(), MultiHydra::new(vec![head_a, head_b, head_c])),
    ]
}

mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_multi_signature() {
        let hydra = build_twin_hydra();
        assert_eq!(hydra.heads.len(), 3);
        assert_eq!(hydra.total_lanes, 15); // 5+5+5
        let sig = hydra.observe(17);
        assert_eq!(sig.bits.len(), 15);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_progressive_resolution() {
        let configs = build_progressive(2);
        assert_eq!(configs.len(), 3);
        assert_eq!(configs[0].1.total_lanes, 5);
        assert_eq!(configs[1].1.total_lanes, 10);
        assert_eq!(configs[2].1.total_lanes, 15);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_lattice_map_basic() {
        let hydra = MultiHydra::new(vec![
            Head::new("test", Champions::baseline(), 2),
        ]);
        let map = hydra.map_lattice(2, 1000);
        assert!(map.total_coprimes > 0);
        assert!(map.total_primes > 0);
        assert!(map.populated_strata > 0);
        // Totals must be consistent
        let sum_c: u32 = map.strata.iter().map(|(_, d)| d.coprime_count).sum();
        assert_eq!(sum_c, map.total_coprimes);
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Orbit Analysis: Multiplicative structure on the CR=18980 torus.
//!
//! Key insight: Each element g ∈ M_H generates an orbit {g^k mod CR : k=1,2,...}
//! with period ord(g) = multiplicative order of g mod CR.
//!
//! Questions:
//! 1. How do orbits partition M_H?
//! 2. Does prime density vary across orbit families?
//! 3. Which generators are primitive roots (maximal order)?
//! 4. Do orbit periods correlate with CRT lane structure?
//!
//! CR = 18980 = 2² × 5 × 13 × 73
//! φ(CR) = 18980 × (1-1/2)(1-1/5)(1-1/13)(1-1/73) = 6912
//! λ(CR) = lcm(λ(4), λ(5), λ(13), λ(73)) = lcm(2, 4, 12, 72) = 72
//!
//! Maximum multiplicative order is λ(CR) = 72, NOT φ(CR) = 6912.
//! This means NO primitive root exists mod CR (since CR is not 1, 2, 4, p^k, or 2p^k).

use crate::crt::{self, gcd, factorize, is_prime, euler_totient, mod_pow};
use crate::monoid::{self, in_monoid, classify_monoid, MonoidClass, M_COPRIME};
use crate::helical::CR;

/// Carmichael's lambda function: the maximum multiplicative order mod n.
/// λ(2^a) = 2^(a-2) for a≥3, 2^(a-1) for a≤2
/// λ(p^a) = p^(a-1)(p-1) for odd prime p
/// λ(n) = lcm(λ(p1^a1), ..., λ(pk^ak))
pub fn carmichael_lambda(n: u128) -> u128 {
    if n <= 2 { return 1; }
    let factors = factorize(n);
    let mut lambda = 1u128;

    for &(p, a) in &factors {
        let lam_pa = if p == 2 {
            if a <= 2 {
                1u128 << (a - 1) // 2^(a-1)
            } else {
                1u128 << (a - 2) // 2^(a-2) for a >= 3
            }
        } else {
            // λ(p^a) = p^(a-1) × (p-1)
            let mut val = p - 1;
            for _ in 1..a {
                val *= p;
            }
            val
        };
        lambda = crt::lcm(lambda, lam_pa);
    }
    lambda
}

/// Compute multiplicative order of g mod n.
/// Returns None if gcd(g, n) ≠ 1.
pub fn multiplicative_order(g: u128, n: u128) -> Option<u128> {
    if gcd(g, n) != 1 { return None; }
    if n == 1 { return Some(1); }

    let lambda = carmichael_lambda(n);

    // The order must divide λ(n). Find the smallest divisor d of λ(n) such that g^d ≡ 1.
    let divisors = divisors_of(lambda);
    for d in divisors {
        if mod_pow(g, d, n) == 1 {
            return Some(d);
        }
    }
    Some(lambda) // should always be found
}

/// Get sorted divisors of n.
pub fn divisors_of(n: u128) -> Vec<u128> {
    let mut divs = Vec::new();
    let mut d = 1u128;
    while d * d <= n {
        if n % d == 0 {
            divs.push(d);
            if d != n / d {
                divs.push(n / d);
            }
        }
        d += 1;
    }
    divs.sort();
    divs
}

/// Compute the full orbit of g mod CR: {g, g², g³, ..., g^ord = 1}
pub fn compute_orbit(g: u128) -> Option<Orbit> {
    let ord = multiplicative_order(g, CR)?;

    let mut theta_sequence = Vec::with_capacity(ord as usize);
    let mut current = 1u128;
    for _ in 0..ord {
        current = crt::mod_mul(current, g % CR, CR);
        theta_sequence.push(current);
    }

    // Verify closure
    assert_eq!(*theta_sequence.last().unwrap(), 1,
        "Orbit of {} did not close: last element = {}", g, theta_sequence.last().unwrap());

    // CRT decomposition of the orbit: track residues mod each factor of CR
    // CR = 4 × 5 × 13 × 73
    let cr_factors = [4u128, 5, 13, 73];
    let sub_orders: Vec<u128> = cr_factors.iter()
        .map(|&m| multiplicative_order(g % m, m).unwrap_or(1))
        .collect();

    Some(Orbit {
        generator: g,
        order: ord,
        theta_sequence,
        sub_orders,
        cr_factors: cr_factors.to_vec(),
    })
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Orbit {
    pub generator: u128,
    pub order: u128,
    pub theta_sequence: Vec<u128>,
    pub sub_orders: Vec<u128>,  // orders mod each CR factor
    pub cr_factors: Vec<u128>,
}

/// Orbit family: group generators by their multiplicative order.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct OrbitFamily {
    pub order: u128,
    pub generators: Vec<u128>,
    pub prime_count: u32,
    pub composite_count: u32,
    pub prime_density: f64,
}

/// Classify all elements of M_H in [2, limit] by orbit family.
pub fn orbit_family_census(limit: u128) -> OrbitFamilyCensus {
    let lambda = carmichael_lambda(CR);
    let possible_orders = divisors_of(lambda);

    let mut families: std::collections::HashMap<u128, OrbitFamily> = std::collections::HashMap::new();

    // Initialize families for all divisors of λ(CR)
    for &ord in &possible_orders {
        families.insert(ord, OrbitFamily {
            order: ord,
            generators: Vec::new(),
            prime_count: 0,
            composite_count: 0,
            prime_density: 0.0,
        });
    }

    let mut total_computed = 0u32;
    let mut order_failures = 0u32;

    for n in 2..=limit {
        if !in_monoid(n) { continue; }
        if gcd(n, CR) != 1 { continue; }

        total_computed += 1;
        match multiplicative_order(n, CR) {
            Some(ord) => {
                let family = families.entry(ord).or_insert(OrbitFamily {
                    order: ord,
                    generators: Vec::new(),
                    prime_count: 0,
                    composite_count: 0,
                    prime_density: 0.0,
                });
                family.generators.push(n);
                if is_prime(n) {
                    family.prime_count += 1;
                } else {
                    family.composite_count += 1;
                }
            }
            None => order_failures += 1,
        }
    }

    // Compute densities
    for family in families.values_mut() {
        let total = family.prime_count + family.composite_count;
        family.prime_density = if total > 0 {
            family.prime_count as f64 / total as f64
        } else { 0.0 };
    }

    // Sort by order
    let mut sorted_families: Vec<OrbitFamily> = families.into_values().collect();
    sorted_families.sort_by_key(|f| f.order);

    OrbitFamilyCensus {
        limit,
        lambda_cr: lambda,
        phi_cr: euler_totient(CR),
        total_computed,
        order_failures,
        families: sorted_families,
        possible_orders,
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct OrbitFamilyCensus {
    pub limit: u128,
    pub lambda_cr: u128,
    pub phi_cr: u128,
    pub total_computed: u32,
    pub order_failures: u32,
    pub families: Vec<OrbitFamily>,
    pub possible_orders: Vec<u128>,
}

/// Deep orbit analysis: for selected generators, compute full orbit
/// and analyze prime density AT EACH θ position.
pub fn orbit_prime_density(generators: &[u128], winding_limit: u128) -> Vec<OrbitPrimeDensity> {
    let mut results = Vec::new();

    for &g in generators {
        let orbit = match compute_orbit(g) {
            Some(o) => o,
            None => continue,
        };

        // For each θ in the orbit, count how many n = θ + k*CR are prime
        let mut theta_prime_counts: Vec<(u128, u32, u32)> = Vec::new(); // (θ, primes, total)

        for &theta in &orbit.theta_sequence {
            let mut primes = 0u32;
            let mut total = 0u32;
            for k in 0..winding_limit {
                let n = theta + k * CR;
                if n < 2 { continue; }
                total += 1;
                if is_prime(n) {
                    primes += 1;
                }
            }
            theta_prime_counts.push((theta, primes, total));
        }

        // Overall density for this orbit vs off-orbit
        let on_orbit_primes: u32 = theta_prime_counts.iter().map(|&(_, p, _)| p).sum();
        let on_orbit_total: u32 = theta_prime_counts.iter().map(|&(_, _, t)| t).sum();

        results.push(OrbitPrimeDensity {
            generator: g,
            order: orbit.order,
            sub_orders: orbit.sub_orders,
            theta_prime_counts,
            on_orbit_primes,
            on_orbit_total,
            density: if on_orbit_total > 0 {
                on_orbit_primes as f64 / on_orbit_total as f64
            } else { 0.0 },
        });
    }
    results
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct OrbitPrimeDensity {
    pub generator: u128,
    pub order: u128,
    pub sub_orders: Vec<u128>,
    pub theta_prime_counts: Vec<(u128, u32, u32)>,
    pub on_orbit_primes: u32,
    pub on_orbit_total: u32,
    pub density: f64,
}

/// Analyze the CRT decomposition of orbits.
/// CR = 4 × 5 × 13 × 73 means each orbit decomposes into sub-orbits
/// on each factor ring. The full order = lcm of sub-orders.
pub fn crt_orbit_decomposition(generators: &[u128]) -> Vec<CRTOrbitDecomp> {
    let cr_factors = [4u128, 5, 13, 73];
    let sub_lambdas: Vec<u128> = cr_factors.iter()
        .map(|&m| carmichael_lambda(m))
        .collect();

    let mut results = Vec::new();

    for &g in generators {
        if gcd(g, CR) != 1 { continue; }

        let sub_residues: Vec<u128> = cr_factors.iter().map(|&m| g % m).collect();
        let sub_orders: Vec<u128> = cr_factors.iter().enumerate()
            .map(|(i, &m)| multiplicative_order(sub_residues[i], m).unwrap_or(0))
            .collect();
        let full_order = sub_orders.iter().copied().reduce(crt::lcm).unwrap_or(1);

        // For each sub-ring, compute the orbit
        let sub_orbits: Vec<Vec<u128>> = cr_factors.iter().enumerate()
            .map(|(i, &m)| {
                let ord = sub_orders[i];
                let mut orbit = Vec::new();
                let mut current = 1u128;
                for _ in 0..ord {
                    current = (current * (g % m)) % m;
                    orbit.push(current);
                }
                orbit
            })
            .collect();

        results.push(CRTOrbitDecomp {
            generator: g,
            is_prime: is_prime(g),
            full_order,
            sub_residues,
            sub_orders: sub_orders.clone(),
            sub_lambdas: sub_lambdas.clone(),
            sub_orbits,
            cr_factors: cr_factors.to_vec(),
            at_max_order: sub_orders.iter().zip(sub_lambdas.iter())
                .all(|(&o, &l)| o == l),
        });
    }
    results
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct CRTOrbitDecomp {
    pub generator: u128,
    pub is_prime: bool,
    pub full_order: u128,
    pub sub_residues: Vec<u128>,
    pub sub_orders: Vec<u128>,
    pub sub_lambdas: Vec<u128>,
    pub sub_orbits: Vec<Vec<u128>>,
    pub cr_factors: Vec<u128>,
    pub at_max_order: bool,
}

/// Artin primitive root analysis:
/// For which primes p is g a primitive root (ord_p(g) = p-1)?
/// Artin's conjecture: every non-square non-{-1} integer is a primitive root
/// for infinitely many primes.
pub fn artin_primitive_root_test(g: u128, prime_limit: u128) -> ArtinReport {
    let mut primes_tested = 0u32;
    let mut is_primitive_root = 0u32;
    let mut not_primitive_root = 0u32;
    let mut primitive_root_primes = Vec::new();

    for p in 2..=prime_limit {
        if !is_prime(p) { continue; }
        if p == g { continue; }
        if gcd(g, p) != 1 { continue; }

        primes_tested += 1;
        let ord = multiplicative_order(g, p).unwrap_or(0);

        if ord == p - 1 {
            is_primitive_root += 1;
            if primitive_root_primes.len() < 30 {
                primitive_root_primes.push(p);
            }
        } else {
            not_primitive_root += 1;
        }
    }

    let density = if primes_tested > 0 {
        is_primitive_root as f64 / primes_tested as f64
    } else { 0.0 };

    // Artin's constant ≈ 0.3739558136...
    let artin_constant = 0.3739558136;

    ArtinReport {
        generator: g,
        primes_tested,
        is_primitive_root_count: is_primitive_root,
        not_primitive_root_count: not_primitive_root,
        density,
        artin_constant,
        ratio_to_artin: density / artin_constant,
        primitive_root_primes,
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ArtinReport {
    pub generator: u128,
    pub primes_tested: u32,
    pub is_primitive_root_count: u32,
    pub not_primitive_root_count: u32,
    pub density: f64,
    pub artin_constant: f64,
    pub ratio_to_artin: f64,
    pub primitive_root_primes: Vec<u128>,
}

/// Orbit collision analysis: when two orbits share θ positions,
/// how does that affect prime density at those positions?
pub fn orbit_collision_analysis(generators: &[u128]) -> CollisionReport {
    let mut theta_to_generators: std::collections::HashMap<u128, Vec<u128>> = std::collections::HashMap::new();

    for &g in generators {
        if let Some(orbit) = compute_orbit(g) {
            for &theta in &orbit.theta_sequence {
                theta_to_generators.entry(theta).or_default().push(g);
            }
        }
    }

    // Count collisions (θ values hit by multiple generators)
    let mut collision_count = 0u32;
    let mut max_collision = 0u32;
    let mut collision_thetas = Vec::new();

    for (&theta, gens) in &theta_to_generators {
        if gens.len() > 1 {
            collision_count += 1;
            if gens.len() as u32 > max_collision {
                max_collision = gens.len() as u32;
            }
            if collision_thetas.len() < 20 {
                collision_thetas.push((theta, gens.clone()));
            }
        }
    }

    // For collision vs non-collision θ values, compare prime density
    // (over several windings)
    let winding_check = 20u128;
    let mut collision_primes = 0u32;
    let mut collision_total = 0u32;
    let mut solo_primes = 0u32;
    let mut solo_total = 0u32;

    for (&theta, gens) in &theta_to_generators {
        for k in 0..winding_check {
            let n = theta + k * CR;
            if n < 2 { continue; }
            let prime = is_prime(n);
            if gens.len() > 1 {
                collision_total += 1;
                if prime { collision_primes += 1; }
            } else {
                solo_total += 1;
                if prime { solo_primes += 1; }
            }
        }
    }

    CollisionReport {
        total_thetas: theta_to_generators.len(),
        collision_count,
        max_collision,
        collision_thetas,
        collision_prime_density: if collision_total > 0 {
            collision_primes as f64 / collision_total as f64
        } else { 0.0 },
        solo_prime_density: if solo_total > 0 {
            solo_primes as f64 / solo_total as f64
        } else { 0.0 },
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct CollisionReport {
    pub total_thetas: usize,
    pub collision_count: u32,
    pub max_collision: u32,
    pub collision_thetas: Vec<(u128, Vec<u128>)>,
    pub collision_prime_density: f64,
    pub solo_prime_density: f64,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_carmichael_lambda_cr() {
        // CR = 2² × 5 × 13 × 73
        // λ(4) = 2, λ(5) = 4, λ(13) = 12, λ(73) = 72
        // λ(CR) = lcm(2, 4, 12, 72) = 72
        assert_eq!(carmichael_lambda(CR), 72);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_no_primitive_root_mod_cr() {
        // Since CR = 4×5×13×73 has more than one odd prime factor,
        // no primitive root exists. Max order = λ(CR) = 72 < φ(CR) = 6912.
        let lambda = carmichael_lambda(CR);
        let phi = euler_totient(CR);
        assert_eq!(lambda, 72);
        assert_eq!(phi, 6912);
        assert!(lambda < phi, "λ(CR) < φ(CR), so no primitive root");
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_order_27() {
        // 27 mod CR: 27^4 ≡ 1 (mod 18980)
        let ord = multiplicative_order(27, CR).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ord, 4);
        assert_eq!(mod_pow(27, 4, CR), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_order_17() {
        let ord = multiplicative_order(17, CR).unwrap();
        // Verify: 17^ord ≡ 1 mod CR
        assert_eq!(mod_pow(17, ord, CR), 1);
        // Verify minimality: 17^(ord-1) ≢ 1
        if ord > 1 {
            assert_ne!(mod_pow(17, ord - 1, CR), 1);
        }
        // Must divide λ(CR) = 72
        assert_eq!(72 % ord, 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_orbit_closure() {
        let orbit = compute_orbit(27).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(orbit.order, 4);
        assert_eq!(*orbit.theta_sequence.last().unwrap(), 1);
        assert_eq!(orbit.theta_sequence, vec![27, 729, 703, 1]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_crt_orbit_decomp() {
        // 27 mod 4 = 3, ord(3, 4) = 2
        // 27 mod 5 = 2, ord(2, 5) = 4
        // 27 mod 13 = 1, ord(1, 13) = 1
        // 27 mod 73 = 27, ord(27, 73) = 4
        // lcm(2, 4, 1, 4) = 4 ✓
        let decomps = crt_orbit_decomposition(&[27]);
        assert_eq!(decomps[0].full_order, 4);
        assert_eq!(decomps[0].sub_orders, vec![2, 4, 1, 4]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_divisors() {
        assert_eq!(divisors_of(12), vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12]);
        assert_eq!(divisors_of(72), vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 72]);
    }
}
```
