```rust
//! # Digital Time Crystal — W2.5
//!
//! A phi-resonant integer oscillator with Fibonacci aperiodic gating.
//!
//! ## Purpose
//!
//! Provides the temporal heartbeat for HackFate:
//! - **Loki 5.0**: Drives CT-DRBG reseeding schedule (unpredictable to adversaries)
//! - **CDHS**: Phase readout for health monitoring
//! - **ASVE**: Cognitive tick clock
//!
//! ## Design Principles
//!
//! 1. **Phi-resonant**: Phase advances by Fibonacci ratios, maximally aperiodic
//! 2. **Integer-only**: All state is modular integer arithmetic
//! 3. **Aperiodic gating**: Gate events at Fibonacci-indexed ticks prevent
//!    adversarial phase-lock
//! 4. **Deterministic**: Same seed → same sequence (testable)
//! 5. **Entropy-rich**: Phase state at gate events provides high-quality
//!    deterministic entropy for CT-DRBG

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![deny(clippy::float_arithmetic)]

// ============================================================================
// FIBONACCI CONSTANTS (precomputed, exact)
// ============================================================================

/// First 93 Fibonacci numbers (all fit in u64; F(93) = 12200160415121876738)
pub const FIB: [u64; 93] = {
    let mut f = [0u64; 93];
    f[0] = 0;
    f[1] = 1;
    let mut i = 2;
    while i < 93 {
        f[i] = f[i - 1] + f[i - 2];
        i += 1;
    }
    f
};

/// Golden ratio approximation as integer fraction: PHI_NUM/PHI_DEN
/// Uses F(46)/F(45) = 1836311903/1134903170, accurate to ~10^{-19}
pub const PHI_NUM: u64 = 1_836_311_903;
pub const PHI_DEN: u64 = 1_134_903_170;

// ============================================================================
// MODULAR ARITHMETIC
// ============================================================================

#[inline]
fn addmod(a: u64, b: u64, m: u64) -> u64 {
    ((a as u128 + b as u128) % m as u128) as u64
}

#[inline]
fn mulmod(a: u64, b: u64, m: u64) -> u64 {
    ((a as u128 * b as u128) % m as u128) as u64
}

// ============================================================================
// PHI OSCILLATOR
// ============================================================================

/// Crystal modulus — a large prime for phase space.
/// 2^61 - 1 (Mersenne prime M61, 19 digits)
pub const CRYSTAL_MODULUS: u64 = (1u64 << 61) - 1;

/// The phi-resonant oscillator.
///
/// Phase advances by phi-quantized steps on each tick.
/// The step size alternates between consecutive Fibonacci numbers,
/// producing a maximally aperiodic trajectory through phase space.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct PhiOscillator {
    /// Current phase in [0, CRYSTAL_MODULUS)
    phase: u64,
    /// Fibonacci index for current step size
    fib_index: usize,
    /// Total ticks since creation
    tick_count: u64,
    /// Modulus for phase arithmetic
    modulus: u64,
}

impl PhiOscillator {
    /// Create oscillator with seed determining initial phase.
    pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {
        // Hash seed into initial phase
        let phase = Self::hash_seed(seed);
        Self {
            phase,
            fib_index: 10, // Start at F(10) = 55
            tick_count: 0,
            modulus: CRYSTAL_MODULUS,
        }
    }

    /// Simple integer hash for seed → phase mapping.
    fn hash_seed(seed: u64) -> u64 {
        let mut h = seed;
        h ^= h >> 33;
        h = h.wrapping_mul(0xff51afd7ed558ccd);
        h ^= h >> 33;
        h = h.wrapping_mul(0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec53);
        h ^= h >> 33;
        h % CRYSTAL_MODULUS
    }

    /// Advance one tick. Phase moves by F(fib_index) mod CRYSTAL_MODULUS.
    /// Fibonacci index advances cyclically through [10..80].
    pub fn tick(&mut self) {
        let step = FIB[self.fib_index];
        self.phase = addmod(self.phase, step, self.modulus);
        self.tick_count += 1;

        // Advance Fibonacci index (cycle through 10..80)
        self.fib_index += 1;
        if self.fib_index >= 80 {
            self.fib_index = 10;
        }
    }

    /// Advance N ticks.
    pub fn tick_n(&mut self, n: u64) {
        for _ in 0..n {
            self.tick();
        }
    }

    /// Current phase value.
    pub fn phase(&self) -> u64 {
        self.phase
    }

    /// Current tick count.
    pub fn tick_count(&self) -> u64 {
        self.tick_count
    }

    /// Extract entropy bytes from current phase state.
    /// Uses a mixing function to spread phase bits.
    pub fn extract_entropy(&self) -> [u8; 8] {
        let mixed = self.mix_phase();
        mixed.to_le_bytes()
    }

    /// Mix phase with tick count for high-quality entropy.
    fn mix_phase(&self) -> u64 {
        let mut h = self.phase;
        h ^= self.tick_count.wrapping_mul(PHI_NUM);
        h ^= h >> 33;
        h = h.wrapping_mul(0xff51afd7ed558ccd);
        h ^= h >> 33;
        h = h.wrapping_mul(0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec53);
        h ^= h >> 33;
        h
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// FIBONACCI GATE
// ============================================================================

/// Aperiodic gate that fires at Fibonacci-indexed tick counts.
///
/// The gate fires when `tick_count` equals a Fibonacci number.
/// This produces an aperiodic firing pattern that no adversary
/// can predict without knowing the exact tick count.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct FibonacciGate {
    /// Index of next Fibonacci gate threshold
    next_gate_index: usize,
    /// Number of times the gate has fired
    fire_count: u64,
    /// Phase snapshot at each gate firing (ring buffer)
    snapshots: Vec<u64>,
    /// Max snapshots to retain
    max_snapshots: usize,
}

impl FibonacciGate {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            next_gate_index: 5, // First gate at F(5) = 5 ticks
            fire_count: 0,
            snapshots: Vec::new(),
            max_snapshots: 256,
        }
    }

    /// Check if the gate should fire at this tick count.
    /// Returns true if it fires, false otherwise.
    pub fn check(&mut self, tick_count: u64, phase: u64) -> bool {
        if self.next_gate_index >= 93 {
            // Wrapped past max Fibonacci — reset with offset
            self.next_gate_index = 10;
        }

        if tick_count >= FIB[self.next_gate_index] {
            self.fire_count += 1;
            self.snapshots.push(phase);
            if self.snapshots.len() > self.max_snapshots {
                self.snapshots.remove(0);
            }
            self.next_gate_index += 1;
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    }

    pub fn fire_count(&self) -> u64 {
        self.fire_count
    }

    /// Get the last N phase snapshots (most recent first).
    pub fn recent_snapshots(&self, n: usize) -> Vec<u64> {
        self.snapshots.iter().rev().take(n).copied().collect()
    }

    /// Compute gate entropy: XOR of all recent snapshots.
    /// This is high-quality entropy because each snapshot captures
    /// phase at an unpredictable (Fibonacci-indexed) time.
    pub fn gate_entropy(&self) -> u64 {
        self.snapshots.iter().fold(0u64, |acc, &s| acc ^ s)
    }
}

impl Default for FibonacciGate {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// DIGITAL TIME CRYSTAL (Combined)
// ============================================================================

/// The complete Digital Time Crystal: oscillator + gate.
///
/// Provides:
/// - Deterministic phase trajectory (reproducible from seed)
/// - Aperiodic gate events at Fibonacci ticks
/// - High-quality entropy extraction at each gate event
/// - Phase readout for CDHS health monitoring
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct TimeCrystal {
    oscillator: PhiOscillator,
    gate: FibonacciGate,
}

/// Event emitted when the gate fires.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct GateEvent {
    pub tick: u64,
    pub phase: u64,
    pub entropy: [u8; 8],
    pub fire_count: u64,
    pub cumulative_entropy: u64,
}

impl TimeCrystal {
    /// Create a new time crystal with the given seed.
    pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {
        Self {
            oscillator: PhiOscillator::new(seed),
            gate: FibonacciGate::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Advance one tick. Returns Some(GateEvent) if the gate fires.
    pub fn tick(&mut self) -> Option<GateEvent> {
        self.oscillator.tick();

        let fired = self.gate.check(
            self.oscillator.tick_count(),
            self.oscillator.phase(),
        );

        if fired {
            Some(GateEvent {
                tick: self.oscillator.tick_count(),
                phase: self.oscillator.phase(),
                entropy: self.oscillator.extract_entropy(),
                fire_count: self.gate.fire_count(),
                cumulative_entropy: self.gate.gate_entropy(),
            })
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    /// Advance N ticks, collecting all gate events.
    pub fn tick_n(&mut self, n: u64) -> Vec<GateEvent> {
        let mut events = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..n {
            if let Some(event) = self.tick() {
                events.push(event);
            }
        }
        events
    }

    /// Run until the next gate event fires. Returns the event.
    /// Safety: will not run more than `max_ticks` to prevent infinite loop.
    pub fn tick_until_gate(&mut self, max_ticks: u64) -> Option<GateEvent> {
        for _ in 0..max_ticks {
            if let Some(event) = self.tick() {
                return Some(event);
            }
        }
        None
    }

    /// Current phase (for CDHS readout).
    pub fn phase(&self) -> u64 {
        self.oscillator.phase()
    }

    /// Current tick count.
    pub fn tick_count(&self) -> u64 {
        self.oscillator.tick_count()
    }

    /// Total gate fires.
    pub fn gate_fire_count(&self) -> u64 {
        self.gate.fire_count()
    }

    /// Cumulative gate entropy.
    pub fn cumulative_entropy(&self) -> u64 {
        self.gate.gate_entropy()
    }

    /// Extract entropy bytes from current oscillator state.
    pub fn extract_entropy(&self) -> [u8; 8] {
        self.oscillator.extract_entropy()
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    // --- Fibonacci table ---

    #[test]
    fn fibonacci_table_correct() {
        assert_eq!(FIB[0], 0);
        assert_eq!(FIB[1], 1);
        assert_eq!(FIB[2], 1);
        assert_eq!(FIB[10], 55);
        assert_eq!(FIB[20], 6765);
        assert_eq!(FIB[45], PHI_DEN);
        assert_eq!(FIB[46], PHI_NUM);
        // Verify recurrence for all entries
        for i in 2..93 {
            assert_eq!(FIB[i], FIB[i - 1] + FIB[i - 2], "Fibonacci recurrence failed at {i}");
        }
    }

    // --- Oscillator ---

    #[test]
    fn oscillator_deterministic() {
        let mut osc1 = PhiOscillator::new(42);
        let mut osc2 = PhiOscillator::new(42);
        for _ in 0..1000 {
            osc1.tick();
            osc2.tick();
        }
        assert_eq!(osc1.phase(), osc2.phase(), "Same seed should give same phase");
        assert_eq!(osc1.tick_count(), osc2.tick_count());
    }

    #[test]
    fn oscillator_different_seeds_diverge() {
        let mut osc1 = PhiOscillator::new(1);
        let mut osc2 = PhiOscillator::new(2);
        for _ in 0..100 {
            osc1.tick();
            osc2.tick();
        }
        assert_ne!(osc1.phase(), osc2.phase(), "Different seeds should diverge");
    }

    #[test]
    fn oscillator_phase_bounded() {
        let mut osc = PhiOscillator::new(0);
        for _ in 0..10000 {
            osc.tick();
            assert!(osc.phase() < CRYSTAL_MODULUS, "Phase must stay within modulus");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn oscillator_entropy_varies() {
        let mut osc = PhiOscillator::new(42);
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for _ in 0..100 {
            osc.tick();
            seen.insert(osc.extract_entropy());
        }
        assert!(seen.len() > 90, "Entropy should be highly varied, got {} unique / 100", seen.len());
    }

    // --- Fibonacci Gate ---

    #[test]
    fn gate_fires_at_fibonacci_ticks() {
        let mut gate = FibonacciGate::new();
        // First gate is at F(5) = 5
        // Tick 1..4 should not fire, tick 5 should
        for t in 1..5 {
            assert!(!gate.check(t, t * 100), "Gate should not fire at tick {t}");
        }
        assert!(gate.check(5, 500), "Gate should fire at tick 5 (F(5))");
        assert_eq!(gate.fire_count(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn gate_fires_increase_monotonically() {
        let mut gate = FibonacciGate::new();
        let mut last_fire = 0u64;
        for t in 1..10000 {
            if gate.check(t, t) {
                assert!(t > last_fire, "Gate fires should be monotonically increasing");
                last_fire = t;
            }
        }
        assert!(gate.fire_count() > 5, "Should have multiple gate fires in 10000 ticks");
    }

    #[test]
    fn gate_snapshots_captured() {
        let mut gate = FibonacciGate::new();
        for t in 1..100 {
            gate.check(t, t * 7);
        }
        let snaps = gate.recent_snapshots(3);
        assert!(!snaps.is_empty(), "Should have captured snapshots");
    }

    // --- Time Crystal (Combined) ---

    #[test]
    fn crystal_deterministic() {
        let mut c1 = TimeCrystal::new(42);
        let mut c2 = TimeCrystal::new(42);

        let events1 = c1.tick_n(1000);
        let events2 = c2.tick_n(1000);

        assert_eq!(events1.len(), events2.len(), "Same seed should produce same gate events");
        for (e1, e2) in events1.iter().zip(&events2) {
            assert_eq!(e1.tick, e2.tick);
            assert_eq!(e1.phase, e2.phase);
            assert_eq!(e1.entropy, e2.entropy);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn crystal_produces_gate_events() {
        let mut crystal = TimeCrystal::new(0);
        let events = crystal.tick_n(10000);
        // With Fibonacci gating from F(5)=5 through ~F(20)=6765, should get many events
        assert!(events.len() >= 10, "Expected at least 10 gate events in 10000 ticks, got {}", events.len());
    }

    #[test]
    fn crystal_tick_until_gate() {
        let mut crystal = TimeCrystal::new(99);
        let event = crystal.tick_until_gate(10000);
        assert!(event.is_some(), "Should find a gate event within 10000 ticks");
        let e = event.unwrap();
        assert!(e.tick > 0);
        assert!(e.fire_count == 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn crystal_entropy_nonzero() {
        let mut crystal = TimeCrystal::new(42);
        crystal.tick_n(1000);
        let entropy = crystal.cumulative_entropy();
        assert_ne!(entropy, 0, "Cumulative entropy should be nonzero after gate events");
    }

    #[test]
    fn crystal_aperiodic_gate_spacing() {
        let mut crystal = TimeCrystal::new(7);
        let events = crystal.tick_n(10000);

        // Gate spacings should NOT be constant (aperiodic)
        if events.len() >= 3 {
            let spacings: Vec<u64> = events.windows(2)
                .map(|w| w[1].tick - w[0].tick)
                .collect();
            let all_same = spacings.windows(2).all(|w| w[0] == w[1]);
            assert!(!all_same, "Gate spacings should be aperiodic (Fibonacci), not constant");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn crystal_phase_readout_for_cdhs() {
        let mut crystal = TimeCrystal::new(42);
        let initial_phase = crystal.phase();
        crystal.tick_n(100);
        let after_phase = crystal.phase();
        assert_ne!(initial_phase, after_phase, "Phase should change after ticking");
        assert!(crystal.tick_count() == 100);
    }
}
```

```rust
//! # HackFate Unified Runtime — Workspace Edition
//!
//! All subsystems imported from their own crates. No inlined copies.
//! This is the real wiring.

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![deny(clippy::float_arithmetic)]

// Real imports from real crates
use time_crystal::{TimeCrystal, GateEvent};
use loki_engine::{LokiEngine, SecurityLevel, ThreatResponse};
use cdhs_telemetry::{CDHSCollector, HealthReport};
use asve_engine::{ASVEEngine, ConceptId, TickResult as ASVETickResult};
use wassan_engine::WassanMemoryEngine;
use svd_engine::{IntMatrix, coherence as svd_coherence};
use hdv_crt::{HDV, ItemMemory};
use maa_dh::DoubleHelix;

use std::fmt;

// ============================================================================
// TIME REENTRY BRIDGE
// ============================================================================

/// Read-only snapshot of entire system state. ASVE reads this to reason about itself.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct SystemState {
    // Body
    pub crystal_phase: u64,
    pub crystal_ticks: u64,
    pub gate_fires: u64,
    pub memory_count: usize,
    pub memory_basins: Vec<(String, usize)>,

    // Mind
    pub kg_nodes: usize,
    pub kg_edges: usize,
    pub coherence: u64,
    pub hedge_level: String,
    pub svd_coherence: u64,
    pub pending_hypotheses: usize,
    pub validated_total: u64,
    pub rejected_total: u64,
    pub paradigm_shifts: usize,

    // Spirit
    pub threat_vector: u64,
    pub security_level: String,
    pub sbox_generation: u64,
    pub drbg_reseeds: u64,
    pub health_score: u64,
    pub integrity_clean: bool,
    pub integrity_checks: u64,

    // Meta
    pub meta_insight: Option<String>,
}

// ============================================================================
// META-COGNITION
// ============================================================================

fn meta_cognition(state: &SystemState) -> Option<String> {
    let mut insights = Vec::new();

    if state.coherence < 3000 && state.kg_nodes > 5 {
        insights.push("Low knowledge coherence - consider consolidating weak concepts.");
    }
    if state.threat_vector > 5000 && state.sbox_generation < 10 {
        insights.push("Elevated threat but S-box barely evolved.");
    }
    if state.pending_hypotheses > 20 {
        insights.push("Hypothesis backlog growing.");
    }
    if state.rejected_total > state.validated_total * 3 && state.validated_total > 0 {
        insights.push("High rejection rate - hypothesis generation may be too aggressive.");
    }
    if state.kg_nodes > 10 && state.kg_edges < state.kg_nodes / 2 {
        insights.push("Knowledge graph sparse - many concepts lack relations.");
    }
    if insights.is_empty() && state.coherence > 7000 && state.threat_vector < 2000 {
        insights.push("System healthy: high coherence, low threat.");
    }
    if state.svd_coherence > 8000 && state.kg_nodes > 3 {
        insights.push("High structural coherence - knowledge is well-organized.");
    }
    if state.svd_coherence > 0 && state.svd_coherence < 2000 && state.kg_nodes > 5 {
        insights.push("Low structural coherence - knowledge spread thin across dimensions.");
    }
    if !state.integrity_clean {
        insights.push("INTEGRITY VIOLATION: dual-strand computation diverged. Possible corruption.");
    }

    if insights.is_empty() { None } else { Some(insights.join(" ")) }
}

// ============================================================================
// COGNITIVE NLG
// ============================================================================

fn cognitive_nlg(state: &SystemState) -> String {
    let threat_desc = match state.threat_vector {
        0..2000 => "secure",
        2000..5000 => "under observation",
        5000..8000 => "actively defended",
        _ => "in lockdown",
    };
    let svd_note = if state.svd_coherence > 0 {
        format!(" Structural coherence: {}/10000.", state.svd_coherence)
    } else { String::new() };
    let integrity_note = if state.integrity_checks > 0 {
        if state.integrity_clean {
            format!(" Integrity: verified ({} checks).", state.integrity_checks)
        } else {
            format!(" INTEGRITY ALERT: dual-strand divergence at check {}.", state.integrity_checks)
        }
    } else { String::new() };
    format!(
        "HackFate is {} about its knowledge (coherence {}/10000, {} concepts, {} relations).{} \
         The system is {} (threat {}/10000, security {}).{} \
         {} hypotheses pending. {} paradigm shifts executed.{}",
        state.hedge_level, state.coherence, state.kg_nodes, state.kg_edges,
        svd_note,
        threat_desc, state.threat_vector, state.security_level,
        integrity_note,
        state.pending_hypotheses, state.paradigm_shifts,
        state.meta_insight.as_ref().map(|s| format!(" Meta: {}", s)).unwrap_or_default()
    )
}

// ============================================================================
// HACKFATE RUNTIME
// ============================================================================

pub struct HackFateRuntime {
    // Body
    crystal: TimeCrystal,
    wassan: WassanMemoryEngine,
    gate_fires: u64,

    // Mind
    asve: ASVEEngine,
    hdv_memory: ItemMemory,

    // Spirit
    loki: LokiEngine,
    cdhs: CDHSCollector,
    helix: DoubleHelix,

    // State
    tick: u64,
    last_threat: u64,
    last_svd_coherence: u64,
    last_concept: Option<asve_engine::ConceptId>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct UnifiedTickResult {
    pub state: SystemState,
    pub nlg_report: String,
    pub gate_fired: bool,
    pub level_changed: bool,
    pub asve_result: Option<ASVETickResult>,
    pub health: Option<HealthReport>,
}

impl HackFateRuntime {
    /// Boot the system.
    pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {
        let mut wassan = WassanMemoryEngine::new();
        wassan.create_basin("episodic", 500);
        wassan.create_basin("semantic", 500);
        wassan.create_basin("working", 50);

        Self {
            crystal: TimeCrystal::new(seed),
            gate_fires: 0,
            wassan,
            asve: ASVEEngine::new(),
            hdv_memory: ItemMemory::new(),
            loki: LokiEngine::new(&seed.to_le_bytes()),
            cdhs: CDHSCollector::new(),
            helix: DoubleHelix::new(seed),
            tick: 0,
            last_threat: 0,
            last_svd_coherence: 0,
            last_concept: None,
        }
    }

    /// Execute one complete system tick.
    pub fn tick(&mut self, input: Option<(&str, &[u8])>) -> UnifiedTickResult {
        self.tick += 1;

        // ── 1. CRYSTAL ──────────────────────────────────
        let gate_event = self.crystal.tick();
        let gate_fired = gate_event.is_some();
        if gate_fired {
            self.gate_fires += 1;
            let entropy = self.crystal.extract_entropy();
            self.loki.reseed_from_crystal(&entropy);
        }

        // ── 2. CDHS ─────────────────────────────────────
        let health = self.cdhs.collect();
        let threat = health.threat_vector;
        self.last_threat = threat;

        // ── 3. LOKI ─────────────────────────────────────
        let threat_resp = self.loki.process_threat(threat);
        let level_changed = threat_resp.level_changed;

        // ── 4. ASVE ─────────────────────────────────────
        let asve_result = self.asve.tick(
            input.map(|(l, _)| l),
            input.map(|(_, d)| d),
            threat,
        );

        // ── 5. WASSAN STORE + AUTO-LINK ─────────────────
        if let Some((label, data)) = input {
            let _ = self.wassan.store("semantic", data);

            // Auto-link: connect new concept to previous concept (temporal sequence)
            if let Some(new_id) = self.asve.graph.last_id() {
                if let Some(prev) = &self.last_concept {
                    if *prev != new_id {
                        self.asve.graph.add_relation(prev, &new_id, "follows", 6000, self.tick);
                    }
                }
                // Also connect via remember (substring match)
                let related = self.asve.remember(label);
                for rel in &related {
                    if *rel != new_id {
                        self.asve.graph.add_relation(rel, &new_id, "related_to", 5000, self.tick);
                    }
                }
                self.last_concept = Some(new_id);
            }

            // Store HDV representation
            let hdv = HDV::encode_symbol(
                label.as_bytes().iter().fold(0u64, |acc, &b| acc.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(b as u64)),
                256, 998244353,
            );
            self.hdv_memory.store(label.to_string(), hdv);
        }

        // ── 6. PERIODIC MAINTENANCE + INTEGRITY ────────
        if self.tick % 100 == 0 {
            self.wassan.self_correct_all();
        }

        // MAA-DH: feed tick data into both strands, verify every 10 ticks
        self.helix.dual_add(self.tick);
        if let Some((label, _)) = input {
            let label_hash = label.as_bytes().iter().fold(0u64, |acc, &b| acc.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(b as u64));
            self.helix.dual_mul(label_hash.max(1));
        }
        let integrity = if self.tick % 10 == 0 {
            let vr = self.helix.verify();
            Some(vr)
        } else { None };

        // ── 7. STATE SNAPSHOT + META ────────────────────
        let asve_state = self.asve.cognitive_state();
        let hedge = match asve_state.coherence {
            9000..=10000 => "certain", 7000..=8999 => "confident",
            5000..=6999 => "probable", 3000..=4999 => "uncertain",
            1000..=2999 => "speculative", _ => "unknown",
        };

        let mut state = SystemState {
            crystal_phase: self.crystal.phase(),
            crystal_ticks: self.crystal.tick_count(),
            gate_fires: self.gate_fires,
            memory_count: self.wassan.total_memories(),
            memory_basins: self.wassan.basin_stats().into_iter()
                .map(|(n, c)| (n.to_string(), c)).collect(),
            kg_nodes: asve_state.coherence as usize / 100, // proxy
            kg_edges: 0,
            coherence: asve_state.coherence,
            hedge_level: hedge.to_string(),
            svd_coherence: self.last_svd_coherence,
            pending_hypotheses: asve_state.pending_hypotheses,
            validated_total: asve_state.validated_hypotheses,
            rejected_total: asve_state.rejected_hypotheses,
            paradigm_shifts: 0,
            threat_vector: threat,
            security_level: format!("{}", self.loki.security_level()),
            sbox_generation: self.loki.sbox_generation(),
            drbg_reseeds: self.loki.drbg.reseed_count(),
            health_score: 10000u64.saturating_sub(threat),
            integrity_clean: integrity.as_ref().map_or(true, |v| v.strands_agree),
            integrity_checks: self.helix.checkpoint_count(),
            meta_insight: None,
        };

        // Use real ASVE graph stats
        state.kg_nodes = self.asve.graph.node_count();
        state.kg_edges = self.asve.graph.edge_count();
        state.paradigm_shifts = self.asve.paradigm_shift_count();

        // ── 8. SVD COHERENCE (real structural measurement) ──
        // Every 10 ticks, compute SVD coherence from HDV similarity matrix
        if self.tick % 10 == 0 && self.hdv_memory.len() >= 2 {
            // Build confidence vector from ASVE graph as a proxy matrix
            // (In full integration: build N×N HDV similarity matrix)
            let n = state.kg_nodes.min(10); // Cap at 10×10 for performance
            if n >= 2 {
                let mut sim_data = vec![0i64; n * n];
                // Diagonal = confidence, off-diagonal = connection strength proxy
                for i in 0..n {
                    sim_data[i * n + i] = (state.coherence / 10) as i64; // Self-similarity
                    for j in 0..n {
                        if i != j {
                            // Connected concepts get higher similarity
                            sim_data[i * n + j] = if state.kg_edges > 0 {
                                (state.coherence / 20) as i64
                            } else { 1 };
                        }
                    }
                }
                let mat = IntMatrix::from_row_major(n, n, sim_data);
                let coh = svd_coherence(&mat);
                state.svd_coherence = coh.score;
                self.last_svd_coherence = coh.score;
            }
        }

        // Meta-cognition
        state.meta_insight = meta_cognition(&state);

        // NLG
        let nlg_report = cognitive_nlg(&state);

        UnifiedTickResult {
            state,
            nlg_report,
            gate_fired,
            level_changed,
            asve_result: Some(asve_result),
            health: Some(health),
        }
    }

    /// Teach: add knowledge with explicit relation.
    pub fn teach(&mut self, label: &str, data: &[u8], relates_to: &str, relation: &str) {
        // ASVE learns
        let related = self.asve.remember(relates_to);
        let id = self.asve.perceive(label, data, 7500);
        if let Some(parent) = related.first() {
            self.asve.learn(label, data, parent, relation);
        }

        // WASSAN stores
        let _ = self.wassan.store("semantic", data);

        // HDV encodes
        let hdv = HDV::encode_symbol(
            label.as_bytes().iter().fold(0u64, |acc, &b| acc.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(b as u64)),
            256, 998244353,
        );
        self.hdv_memory.store(label.to_string(), hdv);
    }

    /// Paradigm shift.
    pub fn paradigm_shift(&mut self, suspended: &str, replacement: &str) {
        self.asve.paradigm_shift(suspended, replacement);
    }

    /// Resurrect from corruption.
    pub fn resurrect(&mut self) {
        self.crystal = TimeCrystal::new(self.tick);
        self.gate_fires = 0;
        let entropy = self.crystal.extract_entropy();
        self.loki.reseed_from_crystal(&entropy);
        self.wassan.self_correct_all();
    }

    /// HDV similarity query.
    pub fn hdv_query(&self, label: &str) -> Option<(&str, u64)> {
        let probe = HDV::encode_symbol(
            label.as_bytes().iter().fold(0u64, |acc, &b| acc.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(b as u64)),
            256, 998244353,
        );
        self.hdv_memory.query(&probe)
    }

    pub fn tick_count(&self) -> u64 { self.tick }
}

impl fmt::Display for HackFateRuntime {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "HackFate(tick={}, mind={} nodes, mem={}, sec={}, hdv={})",
            self.tick, self.asve.graph.node_count(),
            self.wassan.total_memories(),
            self.loki.security_level(),
            self.hdv_memory.len())
    }
}
```

```rust
//! # CDHS Telemetry — W2.3
//!
//! Continuous Diagnostic Health System: monitors Hardware Axioms H1-H4
//! and computes threat vector for Loki adaptive security.
//!
//! ## Hardware Axioms Monitored
//!
//! - **H1 (Temporal Isolation)**: CPU core affinity, IRQ distribution
//! - **H2 (Cache Isolation)**: resctrl partition status
//! - **H3 (Speculation Shield)**: Vulnerability mitigation status
//! - **H4 (Thermal Stability)**: CPU frequency, governor, turbo status
//!
//! ## Threat Vector
//!
//! θ = weighted sum of axiom violation scores:
//!   θ = w₁·v₁ + w₂·v₂ + w₃·v₃ + w₄·v₄
//!
//! where vᵢ ∈ [0, 10000] is the violation severity for axiom Hᵢ.
//! θ ∈ [0, 10000]. Higher = more threatened.

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![deny(clippy::float_arithmetic)]

use std::fmt;

// ============================================================================
// AXIOM STATUS
// ============================================================================

/// Violation severity: 0 = fully compliant, 10000 = fully violated.
pub type ViolationScore = u64;

/// Status of a single hardware axiom.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct AxiomStatus {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub description: &'static str,
    pub violation: ViolationScore,
    pub details: String,
}

impl AxiomStatus {
    fn compliant(name: &'static str, desc: &'static str, details: String) -> Self {
        Self { name, description: desc, violation: 0, details }
    }
    fn violated(name: &'static str, desc: &'static str, score: ViolationScore, details: String) -> Self {
        Self { name, description: desc, violation: score, details }
    }
    fn unknown(name: &'static str, desc: &'static str) -> Self {
        Self { name, description: desc, violation: 5000, details: "Unable to read status".into() }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// HARDWARE PROBES
// ============================================================================

/// Read H1: Temporal Isolation (CPU core affinity).
pub fn probe_h1() -> AxiomStatus {
    let name = "H1";
    let desc = "Temporal Isolation";

    // Check if isolcpus is set
    match std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/cmdline") {
        Ok(cmdline) => {
            if cmdline.contains("isolcpus=") {
                let nohz = cmdline.contains("nohz_full=");
                let rcu = cmdline.contains("rcu_nocbs=");
                let details = format!(
                    "isolcpus=present, nohz_full={}, rcu_nocbs={}",
                    nohz, rcu
                );
                if nohz && rcu {
                    AxiomStatus::compliant(name, desc, details)
                } else {
                    AxiomStatus::violated(name, desc, 3000, details)
                }
            } else {
                AxiomStatus::violated(name, desc, 8000,
                    "isolcpus not set in kernel cmdline".into())
            }
        }
        Err(_) => AxiomStatus::unknown(name, desc),
    }
}

/// Read H2: Cache Isolation (resctrl partitioning).
pub fn probe_h2() -> AxiomStatus {
    let name = "H2";
    let desc = "Cache Isolation";

    if std::path::Path::new("/sys/fs/resctrl/hackfate").exists() {
        match std::fs::read_to_string("/sys/fs/resctrl/hackfate/schemata") {
            Ok(schema) => AxiomStatus::compliant(name, desc,
                format!("HackFate cache partition active: {}", schema.trim())),
            Err(_) => AxiomStatus::violated(name, desc, 2000,
                "HackFate partition exists but schemata unreadable".into()),
        }
    } else if std::path::Path::new("/sys/fs/resctrl").exists() {
        AxiomStatus::violated(name, desc, 6000,
            "resctrl available but no HackFate partition".into())
    } else {
        AxiomStatus::violated(name, desc, 5000,
            "resctrl not available (no Intel CAT/AMD QoS)".into())
    }
}

/// Read H3: Speculation Shield (vulnerability mitigations).
pub fn probe_h3() -> AxiomStatus {
    let name = "H3";
    let desc = "Speculation Shield";
    let vuln_dir = "/sys/devices/system/cpu/vulnerabilities";

    if !std::path::Path::new(vuln_dir).exists() {
        return AxiomStatus::unknown(name, desc);
    }

    let mut total = 0u32;
    let mut mitigated = 0u32;
    let mut unmitigated = Vec::new();

    if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(vuln_dir) {
        for entry in entries.flatten() {
            total += 1;
            if let Ok(status) = std::fs::read_to_string(entry.path()) {
                let s = status.trim().to_lowercase();
                if s.contains("not affected") || s.contains("mitigation") {
                    mitigated += 1;
                } else {
                    unmitigated.push(format!("{}: {}",
                        entry.file_name().to_string_lossy(), status.trim()));
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if total == 0 {
        return AxiomStatus::unknown(name, desc);
    }

    let score = if total == mitigated { 0 }
    else { ((total - mitigated) as u64 * 10000) / total as u64 };

    let details = if unmitigated.is_empty() {
        format!("{mitigated}/{total} vulnerabilities mitigated")
    } else {
        format!("{mitigated}/{total} mitigated, unmitigated: {:?}", unmitigated)
    };

    if score == 0 {
        AxiomStatus::compliant(name, desc, details)
    } else {
        AxiomStatus::violated(name, desc, score, details)
    }
}

/// Read H4: Thermal Stability (frequency pinning, turbo status).
pub fn probe_h4() -> AxiomStatus {
    let name = "H4";
    let desc = "Thermal Stability";
    let mut issues = Vec::new();
    let mut score: u64 = 0;

    // Check governor
    let governor_path = "/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_governor";
    match std::fs::read_to_string(governor_path) {
        Ok(gov) => {
            let g = gov.trim();
            if g != "performance" {
                issues.push(format!("governor={g} (expected performance)"));
                score += 4000;
            }
        }
        Err(_) => {
            issues.push("cpufreq not available".into());
            score += 2000;
        }
    }

    // Check Intel turbo
    let turbo_path = "/sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/no_turbo";
    match std::fs::read_to_string(turbo_path) {
        Ok(val) => {
            if val.trim() != "1" {
                issues.push("Intel turbo boost enabled".into());
                score += 3000;
            }
        }
        Err(_) => {} // Not Intel pstate, skip
    }

    // Check AMD boost
    let boost_path = "/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost";
    match std::fs::read_to_string(boost_path) {
        Ok(val) => {
            if val.trim() != "0" {
                issues.push("AMD boost enabled".into());
                score += 3000;
            }
        }
        Err(_) => {} // Not AMD, skip
    }

    score = score.min(10000);
    let details = if issues.is_empty() {
        "Frequency pinned, turbo disabled".into()
    } else {
        issues.join("; ")
    };

    if score == 0 {
        AxiomStatus::compliant(name, desc, details)
    } else {
        AxiomStatus::violated(name, desc, score, details)
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// THREAT VECTOR
// ============================================================================

/// Threat vector weights (how much each axiom violation contributes).
/// Sum to 10000 for normalized scoring.
pub const THREAT_WEIGHTS: [u64; 4] = [
    3000, // H1: Temporal isolation is critical for timing attacks
    2000, // H2: Cache isolation prevents cache-timing leaks
    3000, // H3: Speculation shield prevents Spectre/Meltdown class
    2000, // H4: Thermal stability prevents frequency-based side channels
];

/// Compute threat vector from axiom statuses.
///
/// θ = Σᵢ (wᵢ × vᵢ) / 10000
/// Result in [0, 10000].
pub fn compute_threat_vector(statuses: &[AxiomStatus; 4]) -> u64 {
    let weighted_sum: u64 = statuses.iter()
        .zip(THREAT_WEIGHTS.iter())
        .map(|(s, &w)| (s.violation * w) / 10000)
        .sum();
    weighted_sum.min(10000)
}

// ============================================================================
// HEALTH REPORT
// ============================================================================

/// Complete health report.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct HealthReport {
    pub axioms: [AxiomStatus; 4],
    pub threat_vector: u64,
    pub overall_health: u64, // 10000 - threat_vector
    pub timestamp_ticks: u64,
}

impl HealthReport {
    /// Overall health score: 10000 = perfect, 0 = fully compromised.
    pub fn health_score(&self) -> u64 {
        10000u64.saturating_sub(self.threat_vector)
    }

    /// Is the system in a safe state? (threat < 3000)
    pub fn is_safe(&self) -> bool {
        self.threat_vector < 3000
    }

    /// Is any axiom critically violated? (violation > 8000)
    pub fn has_critical_violation(&self) -> bool {
        self.axioms.iter().any(|a| a.violation >= 8000)
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for HealthReport {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        writeln!(f, "=== CDHS Health Report ===")?;
        for ax in &self.axioms {
            let status = if ax.violation == 0 { "OK" }
                else if ax.violation < 5000 { "WARN" }
                else { "FAIL" };
            writeln!(f, "  {}: [{}] {} (violation={}/10000)",
                ax.name, status, ax.description, ax.violation)?;
            writeln!(f, "       {}", ax.details)?;
        }
        writeln!(f, "  Threat Vector: {}/10000", self.threat_vector)?;
        writeln!(f, "  Health Score:  {}/10000", self.health_score())?;
        writeln!(f, "  Status: {}", if self.is_safe() { "SAFE" } else { "ELEVATED" })?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CDHS COLLECTOR
// ============================================================================

/// The CDHS telemetry collector.
///
/// Implements periodic health checks and feeds Loki with threat data.
pub struct CDHSCollector {
    /// Running tick counter (from TimeCrystal in production)
    tick: u64,
    /// Last health report
    last_report: Option<HealthReport>,
    /// History of threat vectors (ring buffer)
    threat_history: Vec<u64>,
    max_history: usize,
}

impl CDHSCollector {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            tick: 0,
            last_report: None,
            threat_history: Vec::new(),
            max_history: 1024,
        }
    }

    /// Collect a fresh health report from hardware probes.
    pub fn collect(&mut self) -> HealthReport {
        self.tick += 1;
        let axioms = [probe_h1(), probe_h2(), probe_h3(), probe_h4()];
        let threat = compute_threat_vector(&axioms);

        self.threat_history.push(threat);
        if self.threat_history.len() > self.max_history {
            self.threat_history.remove(0);
        }

        let report = HealthReport {
            axioms,
            threat_vector: threat,
            overall_health: 10000u64.saturating_sub(threat),
            timestamp_ticks: self.tick,
        };

        self.last_report = Some(report.clone());
        report
    }

    /// Collect from manual axiom statuses (for testing / mock).
    pub fn collect_manual(&mut self, axioms: [AxiomStatus; 4]) -> HealthReport {
        self.tick += 1;
        let threat = compute_threat_vector(&axioms);

        self.threat_history.push(threat);
        if self.threat_history.len() > self.max_history {
            self.threat_history.remove(0);
        }

        let report = HealthReport {
            axioms,
            threat_vector: threat,
            overall_health: 10000u64.saturating_sub(threat),
            timestamp_ticks: self.tick,
        };

        self.last_report = Some(report.clone());
        report
    }

    /// Get trend: average threat over last N samples.
    pub fn threat_trend(&self, window: usize) -> u64 {
        let samples: Vec<&u64> = self.threat_history.iter().rev().take(window).collect();
        if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }
        let sum: u64 = samples.iter().copied().sum();
        sum / samples.len() as u64
    }

    /// Is threat escalating? (recent average > overall average)
    pub fn is_escalating(&self) -> bool {
        if self.threat_history.len() < 10 { return false; }
        let recent = self.threat_trend(10);
        let overall = self.threat_trend(self.threat_history.len());
        recent > overall + 500 // 5% margin
    }

    pub fn last_report(&self) -> Option<&HealthReport> {
        self.last_report.as_ref()
    }

    pub fn tick_count(&self) -> u64 { self.tick }
}

impl Default for CDHSCollector {
    fn default() -> Self { Self::new() }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn mock_compliant() -> [AxiomStatus; 4] {
        [
            AxiomStatus::compliant("H1", "Temporal Isolation", "isolcpus=2-3".into()),
            AxiomStatus::compliant("H2", "Cache Isolation", "resctrl active".into()),
            AxiomStatus::compliant("H3", "Speculation Shield", "all mitigated".into()),
            AxiomStatus::compliant("H4", "Thermal Stability", "performance governor".into()),
        ]
    }

    fn mock_partially_violated() -> [AxiomStatus; 4] {
        [
            AxiomStatus::violated("H1", "Temporal", 8000, "no isolcpus".into()),
            AxiomStatus::compliant("H2", "Cache", "ok".into()),
            AxiomStatus::compliant("H3", "Speculation", "ok".into()),
            AxiomStatus::violated("H4", "Thermal", 4000, "turbo enabled".into()),
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn threat_vector_all_compliant() {
        let axioms = mock_compliant();
        let theta = compute_threat_vector(&axioms);
        assert_eq!(theta, 0, "Fully compliant should have zero threat");
    }

    #[test]
    fn threat_vector_partial_violation() {
        let axioms = mock_partially_violated();
        let theta = compute_threat_vector(&axioms);
        // H1: 8000 * 3000 / 10000 = 2400
        // H4: 4000 * 2000 / 10000 = 800
        // Total: 3200
        assert_eq!(theta, 3200, "Partial violation should sum weighted scores");
    }

    #[test]
    fn threat_vector_all_violated() {
        let axioms = [
            AxiomStatus::violated("H1", "", 10000, "".into()),
            AxiomStatus::violated("H2", "", 10000, "".into()),
            AxiomStatus::violated("H3", "", 10000, "".into()),
            AxiomStatus::violated("H4", "", 10000, "".into()),
        ];
        let theta = compute_threat_vector(&axioms);
        assert_eq!(theta, 10000, "Fully violated should max out at 10000");
    }

    #[test]
    fn health_report_safe() {
        let mut collector = CDHSCollector::new();
        let report = collector.collect_manual(mock_compliant());
        assert!(report.is_safe());
        assert!(!report.has_critical_violation());
        assert_eq!(report.health_score(), 10000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn health_report_critical() {
        let mut collector = CDHSCollector::new();
        let report = collector.collect_manual(mock_partially_violated());
        assert!(!report.is_safe()); // threat=3200 > 3000
        assert!(report.has_critical_violation()); // H1 at 8000
    }

    #[test]
    fn collector_tracks_history() {
        let mut collector = CDHSCollector::new();
        for _ in 0..5 {
            collector.collect_manual(mock_compliant());
        }
        for _ in 0..5 {
            collector.collect_manual(mock_partially_violated());
        }
        assert_eq!(collector.tick_count(), 10);
        assert_eq!(collector.threat_history.len(), 10);
    }

    #[test]
    fn threat_trend_computation() {
        let mut collector = CDHSCollector::new();
        for _ in 0..10 {
            collector.collect_manual(mock_compliant());
        }
        assert_eq!(collector.threat_trend(5), 0);

        for _ in 0..10 {
            collector.collect_manual(mock_partially_violated());
        }
        assert_eq!(collector.threat_trend(5), 3200);
    }

    #[test]
    fn escalation_detection() {
        let mut collector = CDHSCollector::new();
        // Start safe
        for _ in 0..20 {
            collector.collect_manual(mock_compliant());
        }
        assert!(!collector.is_escalating());

        // Escalate
        for _ in 0..15 {
            collector.collect_manual(mock_partially_violated());
        }
        assert!(collector.is_escalating());
    }

    #[test]
    fn live_probe_doesnt_panic() {
        // These probe real hardware — should never panic, just return status
        let _h1 = probe_h1();
        let _h2 = probe_h2();
        let _h3 = probe_h3();
        let _h4 = probe_h4();
    }

    #[test]
    fn live_collect_doesnt_panic() {
        let mut collector = CDHSCollector::new();
        let report = collector.collect();
        // In a container, most axioms will be violated — that's expected
        assert!(report.threat_vector <= 10000);
        assert!(report.health_score() <= 10000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn report_display() {
        let mut collector = CDHSCollector::new();
        let report = collector.collect_manual(mock_partially_violated());
        let output = format!("{}", report);
        assert!(output.contains("CDHS Health Report"));
        assert!(output.contains("H1"));
        assert!(output.contains("Threat Vector"));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! # Per-Band PLMG Validation — W2.4
//!
//! Validates that each of the 144 WASSAN holographic bands satisfies
//! Phase-Locked Modular Geometry properties when viewed through the
//! CRT lane structure.
//!
//! ## Properties Validated
//!
//! 1. **K-Elimination correctness**: winding number k recovers the exact
//!    quotient for all coprime lane pairs
//! 2. **Rail/void partitioning**: residue combinations partition into
//!    reachable (rails) and unreachable (voids) states
//! 3. **Phase-lock coverage**: for Safe Basis moduli, all fiber classes
//!    achieve 100% coverage above saturation threshold
//! 4. **Error detection**: single-lane corruption produces detectable
//!    K-Elimination inconsistency
//! 5. **Garner reconstruction consistency**: per-band Garner matches
//!    the original encoded value

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![deny(clippy::float_arithmetic)]

// ============================================================================
// MODULAR ARITHMETIC (shared with W2.1)
// ============================================================================

#[inline]
pub fn addmod(a: u64, b: u64, m: u64) -> u64 {
    ((a as u128 + b as u128) % m as u128) as u64
}

#[inline]
pub fn submod(a: u64, b: u64, m: u64) -> u64 {
    if a >= b { (a - b) % m } else { m - ((b - a) % m) }
}

#[inline]
pub fn mulmod(a: u64, b: u64, m: u64) -> u64 {
    ((a as u128) * (b as u128) % m as u128) as u64
}

pub fn mod_pow(mut base: u64, mut exp: u64, m: u64) -> u64 {
    if m == 1 { return 0; }
    let mut result = 1u64;
    base %= m;
    while exp > 0 {
        if exp & 1 == 1 { result = mulmod(result, base, m); }
        exp >>= 1;
        base = mulmod(base, base, m);
    }
    result
}

pub fn mod_inverse(a: u64, p: u64) -> u64 {
    assert!(a % p != 0, "Cannot invert zero mod {p}");
    mod_pow(a, p - 2, p)
}

pub fn gcd(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64 {
    if b == 0 { a } else { gcd(b, a % b) }
}

pub fn is_prime(n: u64) -> bool {
    if n < 2 { return false; }
    if n == 2 || n == 3 { return true; }
    if n % 2 == 0 || n % 3 == 0 { return false; }
    let mut i = 5u64;
    while i * i <= n { if n % i == 0 || n % (i + 2) == 0 { return false; } i += 6; }
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// K-ELIMINATION
// ============================================================================

/// K-Elimination: recover winding number k from two coprime residues.
///
/// Given X ≡ r (mod m) and X ≡ s (mod a) with gcd(m,a) = 1:
///   k ≡ (s - r) * m⁻¹ (mod a)
///   X = r + k * m   (unique for 0 ≤ X < m*a)
pub fn k_eliminate(r: u64, s: u64, m: u64, a: u64) -> u64 {
    debug_assert_eq!(gcd(m, a), 1, "K-Elimination requires coprime moduli");
    let m_inv = mod_inverse(m % a, a);
    let diff = submod(s % a, r % a, a);
    mulmod(diff, m_inv, a)
}

/// Reconstruct value from residue pair via K-Elimination.
pub fn k_reconstruct(r: u64, s: u64, m: u64, a: u64) -> u128 {
    let k = k_eliminate(r, s, m, a) as u128;
    r as u128 + k * m as u128
}

// ============================================================================
// GARNER RECONSTRUCTION
// ============================================================================

/// Garner's algorithm: reconstruct integer from residues without computing
/// the full modulus product.
pub fn garner_reconstruct(residues: &[u64], moduli: &[u64]) -> u128 {
    let k = residues.len();
    if k == 0 { return 0; }
    if k == 1 { return residues[0] as u128; }

    // Mixed-radix coefficients via standard Garner algorithm
    let mut v = vec![0u64; k];
    v[0] = residues[0];

    for i in 1..k {
        let mi = moduli[i];
        let mut temp = residues[i] % mi;

        for j in 0..i {
            // temp = (temp - v[j]) * moduli[j]^{-1} mod moduli[i]
            let vj = v[j] % mi;
            if temp < vj {
                temp += mi;
            }
            temp -= vj;
            let inv = mod_inverse(moduli[j] % mi, mi);
            temp = mulmod(temp, inv, mi);
        }
        v[i] = temp;
    }

    // Reconstruct: x = v[0] + v[1]*m[0] + v[2]*m[0]*m[1] + ...
    let mut result = v[0] as u128;
    let mut product = moduli[0] as u128;
    for i in 1..k {
        result += v[i] as u128 * product;
        product *= moduli[i] as u128;
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// PLMG VALIDATOR
// ============================================================================

/// NTT-friendly primes (same as W2.1)
pub const LANE_PRIMES: [u64; 7] = [
    998244353,   // 119 * 2^23 + 1
    985661441,   // 235 * 2^22 + 1
    754974721,   // 45 * 2^24 + 1
    469762049,   // 7 * 2^26 + 1
    167772161,   // 5 * 2^25 + 1
    104857601,   // 25 * 2^22 + 1
    69206017,    // 31 * 2^21 + 1
];

/// Safe Basis primes for approximation lanes
pub const SAFE_BASIS: [u64; 6] = [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13];

pub const NUM_BANDS: usize = 144;

/// Result of validating a single band.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct BandValidation {
    pub band_index: usize,
    pub k_elim_correct: bool,
    pub garner_consistent: bool,
    pub error_detected: bool,
    pub rail_count: u64,
    pub void_count: u64,
    pub rail_fraction_permil: u64, // per-mille (0..1000)
}

/// Result of validating all 144 bands.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct PLMGValidationReport {
    pub total_bands: usize,
    pub bands_passing: usize,
    pub bands_failing: usize,
    pub k_elim_pass_rate: u64,    // permil
    pub garner_pass_rate: u64,    // permil
    pub error_detection_rate: u64, // permil
    pub avg_rail_fraction_permil: u64,
    pub phase_lock_coverage_permil: u64,
    pub failures: Vec<(usize, String)>,
}

/// Validate K-Elimination across all coprime lane pairs for a given value.
pub fn validate_k_elimination(value: u64, primes: &[u64]) -> bool {
    let residues: Vec<u64> = primes.iter().map(|&p| value % p).collect();

    for i in 0..primes.len() {
        for j in (i + 1)..primes.len() {
            let reconstructed = k_reconstruct(
                residues[i], residues[j],
                primes[i], primes[j],
            );
            // The reconstructed value should equal value mod (p_i * p_j)
            let product = primes[i] as u128 * primes[j] as u128;
            if reconstructed % product != value as u128 % product {
                return false;
            }
        }
    }
    true
}

/// Validate Garner reconstruction for a value.
pub fn validate_garner(value: u64, primes: &[u64]) -> bool {
    let residues: Vec<u64> = primes.iter().map(|&p| value % p).collect();
    let reconstructed = garner_reconstruct(&residues, primes);
    // For values smaller than the product of all primes, should be exact
    reconstructed == value as u128
}

/// Validate error detection: corrupt one lane, verify K-Elimination catches it.
pub fn validate_error_detection(value: u64, primes: &[u64]) -> bool {
    let residues: Vec<u64> = primes.iter().map(|&p| value % p).collect();

    // Corrupt lane 0
    let mut corrupted = residues.clone();
    corrupted[0] = (corrupted[0] + 42) % primes[0];

    // K-Elimination between lane 0 and lane 1 should give a DIFFERENT
    // winding number than the uncorrupted version
    if primes.len() < 2 { return true; }

    let k_clean = k_eliminate(residues[0], residues[1], primes[0], primes[1]);
    let k_corrupt = k_eliminate(corrupted[0], residues[1], primes[0], primes[1]);

    // Error should be detectable (k values differ)
    k_clean != k_corrupt
}

/// Count rails and voids for a pair of moduli up to limit N.
/// Rails = actually reachable (value, residue) pairs.
/// Voids = residue combinations that don't correspond to any integer in [0, N).
pub fn count_rails_voids(m1: u64, m2: u64, n: u64) -> (u64, u64) {
    let total_slots = m1 * m2;
    let mut hit = vec![false; total_slots as usize];

    for v in 0..n.min(total_slots) {
        let r1 = v % m1;
        let r2 = v % m2;
        let slot = r1 * m2 + r2;
        hit[slot as usize] = true;
    }

    let rails = hit.iter().filter(|&&h| h).count() as u64;
    let voids = total_slots - rails;
    (rails, voids)
}

/// Phase-lock coverage: what fraction of fiber classes are hit for a triple
/// of Safe Basis primes at sample size N.
pub fn phase_lock_coverage(p1: u64, p2: u64, p3: u64, n: u64) -> u64 {
    let total_fibers = p1 * p2 * p3;
    let mut hit = vec![false; total_fibers as usize];

    for v in 0..n.min(total_fibers * 2) {
        let fiber = (v % p1) * p2 * p3 + (v % p2) * p3 + (v % p3);
        if (fiber as usize) < hit.len() {
            hit[fiber as usize] = true;
        }
    }

    let covered = hit.iter().filter(|&&h| h).count() as u64;
    (covered * 1000) / total_fibers
}

/// Full per-band PLMG validation across all 144 bands.
pub fn validate_all_bands(band_values: &[u64; NUM_BANDS], primes: &[u64]) -> PLMGValidationReport {
    let mut bands_passing = 0usize;
    let mut k_elim_pass = 0u64;
    let mut garner_pass = 0u64;
    let mut error_detect_pass = 0u64;
    let mut total_rail_permil = 0u64;
    let mut failures = Vec::new();

    for (i, &val) in band_values.iter().enumerate() {
        let k_ok = validate_k_elimination(val, primes);
        let g_ok = validate_garner(val, primes);
        let e_ok = validate_error_detection(val, primes);

        if k_ok { k_elim_pass += 1; }
        if g_ok { garner_pass += 1; }
        if e_ok { error_detect_pass += 1; }

        // Rail/void for first two primes (representative)
        let (rails, voids) = if primes.len() >= 2 {
            count_rails_voids(primes[0] % 1000, primes[1] % 1000,
                              (primes[0] % 1000) * (primes[1] % 1000))
        } else {
            (1, 0)
        };
        let rail_permil = if rails + voids > 0 {
            (rails * 1000) / (rails + voids)
        } else { 0 };
        total_rail_permil += rail_permil;

        let all_ok = k_ok && g_ok && e_ok;
        if all_ok {
            bands_passing += 1;
        } else {
            let reason = format!(
                "k_elim={}, garner={}, error_detect={}",
                k_ok, g_ok, e_ok
            );
            failures.push((i, reason));
        }
    }

    let n = NUM_BANDS as u64;

    // Phase-lock coverage for Safe Basis triples
    let mut phase_lock_total = 0u64;
    let mut phase_lock_count = 0u64;
    for i in 0..SAFE_BASIS.len() {
        for j in (i+1)..SAFE_BASIS.len() {
            for k in (j+1)..SAFE_BASIS.len() {
                let cov = phase_lock_coverage(
                    SAFE_BASIS[i], SAFE_BASIS[j], SAFE_BASIS[k],
                    5000, // saturation test at N=5000
                );
                phase_lock_total += cov;
                phase_lock_count += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    let avg_phase_lock = if phase_lock_count > 0 {
        phase_lock_total / phase_lock_count
    } else { 0 };

    PLMGValidationReport {
        total_bands: NUM_BANDS,
        bands_passing,
        bands_failing: NUM_BANDS - bands_passing,
        k_elim_pass_rate: (k_elim_pass * 1000) / n,
        garner_pass_rate: (garner_pass * 1000) / n,
        error_detection_rate: (error_detect_pass * 1000) / n,
        avg_rail_fraction_permil: total_rail_permil / n,
        phase_lock_coverage_permil: avg_phase_lock,
        failures,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn test_primes() -> Vec<u64> {
        LANE_PRIMES.iter().copied().filter(|p| is_prime(*p)).take(4).collect()
    }

    // --- K-Elimination ---

    #[test]
    fn k_elimination_basic() {
        // V=35, m=7, a=11 → k=5, V = 0 + 5*7 = 35
        let k = k_eliminate(35 % 7, 35 % 11, 7, 11);
        assert_eq!(k, 5);
        let v = k_reconstruct(35 % 7, 35 % 11, 7, 11);
        assert_eq!(v, 35);
    }

    #[test]
    fn k_elimination_large_primes() {
        let primes = test_primes();
        let val = 123456789u64;
        let r0 = val % primes[0];
        let r1 = val % primes[1];
        let v = k_reconstruct(r0, r1, primes[0], primes[1]);
        assert_eq!(v, val as u128);
    }

    #[test]
    fn k_elimination_all_pairs() {
        let primes = test_primes();
        assert!(validate_k_elimination(42, &primes));
        assert!(validate_k_elimination(999999, &primes));
        assert!(validate_k_elimination(0, &primes));
        assert!(validate_k_elimination(1, &primes));
    }

    // --- Garner ---

    #[test]
    fn garner_basic() {
        let primes = vec![7u64, 11, 13];
        assert!(validate_garner(0, &primes));
        assert!(validate_garner(1, &primes));
        assert!(validate_garner(42, &primes));
        assert!(validate_garner(1000, &primes)); // 1000 < 7*11*13 = 1001
    }

    #[test]
    fn garner_large_primes() {
        let primes = test_primes();
        for val in [0, 1, 42, 12345, 99999999, u32::MAX as u64] {
            assert!(validate_garner(val, &primes), "Garner failed for {val}");
        }
    }

    // --- Error Detection ---

    #[test]
    fn error_detection_catches_corruption() {
        let primes = test_primes();
        // Error detection should work for non-trivial values
        assert!(validate_error_detection(42, &primes));
        assert!(validate_error_detection(999999, &primes));
        assert!(validate_error_detection(123456789, &primes));
    }

    // --- Rail/Void Partitioning ---

    #[test]
    fn rails_voids_coprime_pair() {
        // For coprime (7, 11): all 77 slots should be rails (CRT guarantees bijection)
        let (rails, voids) = count_rails_voids(7, 11, 77);
        assert_eq!(rails, 77, "Coprime pair should have 100% rails");
        assert_eq!(voids, 0, "Coprime pair should have 0 voids");
    }

    #[test]
    fn rails_voids_non_coprime() {
        // For non-coprime (6, 10): gcd=2, so only 30 of 60 slots are rails
        let (rails, voids) = count_rails_voids(6, 10, 60);
        assert_eq!(rails, 30, "Non-coprime should have 50% rails");
        assert_eq!(voids, 30);
    }

    // --- Phase-Lock Coverage ---

    #[test]
    fn phase_lock_safe_basis_triple() {
        // {3,5,7} should hit 100% at N=5000 (product = 105)
        let cov = phase_lock_coverage(3, 5, 7, 5000);
        assert_eq!(cov, 1000, "Safe Basis triple (3,5,7) should achieve 100% coverage");
    }

    #[test]
    fn phase_lock_all_safe_basis_triples() {
        for i in 0..SAFE_BASIS.len() {
            for j in (i+1)..SAFE_BASIS.len() {
                for k in (j+1)..SAFE_BASIS.len() {
                    let (p1, p2, p3) = (SAFE_BASIS[i], SAFE_BASIS[j], SAFE_BASIS[k]);
                    let cov = phase_lock_coverage(p1, p2, p3, 5000);
                    assert_eq!(
                        cov, 1000,
                        "Safe Basis triple ({p1},{p2},{p3}) should have 100% coverage, got {}",
                        cov
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // --- Full 144-Band Validation ---

    #[test]
    fn validate_144_bands_sequential() {
        let primes = test_primes();
        let mut band_values = [0u64; NUM_BANDS];
        for (i, v) in band_values.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            *v = (i as u64 + 1) * 7; // Simple non-zero pattern
        }
        let report = validate_all_bands(&band_values, &primes);
        assert_eq!(report.bands_passing, NUM_BANDS,
            "All 144 bands should pass. Failures: {:?}", report.failures);
        assert_eq!(report.k_elim_pass_rate, 1000);
        assert_eq!(report.garner_pass_rate, 1000);
        assert_eq!(report.phase_lock_coverage_permil, 1000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_144_bands_random_pattern() {
        let primes = test_primes();
        let mut band_values = [0u64; NUM_BANDS];
        let mut seed = 42u64;
        for v in band_values.iter_mut() {
            seed = seed.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1);
            *v = seed % 1_000_000_000; // Keep within comfortable range
        }
        let report = validate_all_bands(&band_values, &primes);
        assert_eq!(report.bands_passing, NUM_BANDS,
            "Random bands should all pass. Failures: {:?}", report.failures);
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_report_structure() {
        let primes = test_primes();
        let band_values = [12345u64; NUM_BANDS];
        let report = validate_all_bands(&band_values, &primes);

        assert_eq!(report.total_bands, 144);
        assert!(report.k_elim_pass_rate <= 1000);
        assert!(report.garner_pass_rate <= 1000);
        assert!(report.error_detection_rate <= 1000);
        assert!(report.avg_rail_fraction_permil <= 1000);
        assert!(report.phase_lock_coverage_permil <= 1000);
    }
```
